docs.text:
Google review of Trader Joe's (5 out of 5, by Mathy, 4 months ago): Decided to give this place a try since it's close to the beach, and I'm glad I did. I picked up a few things, including juice, snacks, and some dog treats. For a smaller store, they have a surprisingly great selection. I'm assuming it's a newer location in the area, but everything was well-stocked and easy to find.

The staff were friendly, welcoming, and made the experience even better. Special shoutout to the staff member who recommended the truffle potato chips they were excellent I'll definitely be coming back, and next time. I'll probably grab two bags.

docs.title: Review of Trader Joe's
docs.text:
Google review of Trader Joe's (1 out of 5, by Jean Marcel, 2 months ago): I'm one of those TJ's fanatics. However, after more than 35 years of shopping at TJ's, today, I had a bad experience at this location. I walked into the store and, as usual, every time I pass the sample kiosk, I try what's being offered (even though, after all this time, I probably tried everything at TJ's). On the menu today was a Turkish flat bread with a tomato spread. As soon as I placed the small sample in my mouth," I could tell the spread was bad (meaning expired), I told the young woman in a very calm manner "I think this is bad", she replied in a not very polite manner "Maybe it's not to your liking" and exchanged a condescending look with the other young woman in front of her, who appeared to be a Manager or Supervisor, as if I was some kind of male Karen giving her a hard time. So, because she clearly didn't understand, I said it again in a very polite manner " I mean this is bad, meaning it might be expired", and the Manager raised her voice and said, "That's how it is!". I was "okay" and just walked away.
Alright, so here's the thing. First of all, I love food that is tart, even bitter tasting, but I'm old enough to tell the difference between a tart or sour flavor or when the food is bad (once again, meaning expired). Second, even if I'm wrong, if any of those two employees had any customer service skills or were raised to develop anything that remotely resemble people skills. Then, when an older, regular customer, tells them in a polite manner "I think this might be expired", the right reaction should've been to try it and double check the product, not making looks and raise their voice. I, the customer was the one who said "okay" and went my way to de-escalate the situation. And, I simply walked out of the store without shopping and went to Whole Foods, where I'll be shopping more often from now on.

They're all good with a reasonable price.  The staff are nice.  If you don't know where a product is located, they lead you to the product

Google review of Trader Joe's (5 out of 5, by Carmen Molinari, 3 months ago): If you are looking for that neighborhood market where everyone knows your name, then this is the place for you!

Staff here are not only friendly, but they're approachable, and knowledgeable of their products.

If you don't see something that that you are looking for on the shelf, they'll go the extra mile and check their stock in the back of the store, and even look it up in their system to tell you the status of the product, and when it might be available in the store.

If you have a return, they don't try to shame you!

When you reach the register they are warm and efficent.

Everyone genuinely seem like they enjoy working there which really adds to the welcoming atmosphere.

5 stars all the way! *****

docs.text: Google review of Trader Joe's (5 out of 5, by Todd M., 5 months ago): This was our 1st time going to a Trader Joe's. Unfortunately, we don't have the chain in Canada. Too bad because they have a lot of unique items. All the Trader Joe's branded items we purchased were very good quality. This location has a decent selection of fresh produce & everything else we were looking for. They also had an incredible offering of fresh cut flowers. You can buy a prearranged bouquet or make your own. The staff were friendly & helpful, prices were very reasonable, store was clean & they have free underground parking. We'll definitely be back the next time we're in Santa Monica.

docs.text: Google review of Trader Joe's (4 out of 5, by Ellie Richard, 7 months ago): So many colorful organic veggies and fruits - everything looked so fresh. So many new and yummy looking things to try there. Store was very clean. The feesh Pineberries were $5.99 per package and you got so few of them,  it I was wanting to try them I had to go through dozens and dozens of packages to finally find one that didn't have any bruised berries or a sliminess on the bottom of the package. I said something to a gentleman that was stocking in the berry section about the condition of the Pineberries and he said, "yes, ma'am, I will pull all of them off display until we can really look at them. It's possible to save some packages by cleaning out the bad, bruised, slimy ones. I appreciate you telling me. Thank you." I just stood there stunned 😯 I've never seen a person jump on a problem so quickly. They also had a nice wine, beer, and liquor selection, if you're interested.

docs.text: Google review of Trader Joe's (5 out of 5, by Guillaume Bourcy, a year ago): This Trader Joe's boasts an excellent location right in the heart of Santa Monica, offering a great selection of traditional products and groceries known to the brand. The store is situated conveniently, making it easy to pop in. Prices are reasonable, and the staff is both accommodating and helpful. While the parking in the building's garage can fill up quickly during peak hours, access is generally straightforward. The store has a pleasant atmosphere, with numerous nods to Santa Monica, including references to well-known spots and local beaches, adding a nice local touch.

docs.title: Review of Whole Foods Market
docs.text:
Google review of Whole Foods Market (1 out of 5, by tylermccrary1865, 4 months ago): I would like to provide feedback regarding my recent experience at the meat counter that I have been to, many times.

I understand that Whole Foods has a policy requiring certain meat purchases above a specific value or quantity threshold to be held at the front of the store for pickup (which, not even the DTLA has this policy, which even further proves my point for profiling here in SAMO). I am familiar with and respect this policy.

However, during my visit, I observed a customer ahead of me purchase significantly more meat than I did, with a much higher overall  total spend across multiple selections, possibly 5 to 10 times the amount and price of my selection. Despite this, her purchase was handled differently. When I ordered only three steaks, I was immediately subjected to the front-hold procedure.

What concerns me is the inconsistency in how this policy is applied. From my perspective, customers are not being treated equally, and I felt singled out based on assumptions rather than objective application of store policy. If the policy is based on purchase value, quantity, or another measurable standard, it should be applied consistently to all customers.

I also want to note that the employee working the counter appeared to be of the same racial background as the customer ahead of me, while I was a younger customer and was treated differently despite making a substantially smaller purchase. I cannot know the reason for the difference in treatment, but the circumstances left me concerned that factors other than the stated policy may have influenced the decision.

I am not objecting to the policy itself. My concern is the apparent unequal treatment and the feeling that I was profiled while other customers making larger purchases were not subjected to the same process.

I would appreciate clarification on the policy and how Whole Foods ensures it is applied fairly and consistently to all customers.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

docs.title: Review of Ralphs Fresh Fare
docs.text:
Google review of Ralphs Fresh Fare (1 out of 5, by Emily Liu, a month ago): I’m very disappointed with how I was treated by the security guard today.

I normally have no interest in Pokémon cards and honestly know very little about them. I only recently started learning about them because my child was invited to a friend’s birthday party where the kids will be trading Pokémon cards. I was simply trying to understand how these cards and the vending machine work.

Today, I was standing in front of the Pokémon vending machine for no more than five minutes, looking at the products and trying to understand how the machine works. My husband was waiting for me in the parking lot because we thought we could simply come in, make a purchase, and leave. He didn’t even come inside. When I saw that everything was sold out and refreshed screen didn’t work, I stepped away from machine and was texting him to explain what I was seeing on the machine.

The security guard approached me and told me I was “loitering.” I asked him what he meant by “loitering,” and he explained that customers are not supposed to stand in front of the vending machine for an extended period of time. He told me that customers should simply walk by, try the machine, buy something if it is available, and leave if nothing is available.

I was genuinely confused by this because I had been there for only about five minutes, possibly even less, and was simply trying to learn about a product I knew very little about. I was not bothering anyone or doing anything inappropriate. There were no other customers around the machine at the time, and I wasn’t blocking anyone from using it.

I understand that the store has the right to ask customers to leave, but I found the way this was handled unnecessary and uncomfortable. Being approached and labeled as “loitering” when I was simply trying to understand a product as a customer, and had only been standing in front of the machine for a few minutes, was a very disappointing experience.

docs.title: Review of Vons
docs.text:
Google review of Vons (1 out of 5, by Kevin Glover, a month ago): I had a deeply upsetting experience at this Vons today. After paying for every item at the self-checkout and exiting the store, I was approached by a manager and another employee who did not identify herself. They accused me of leaving without paying for all of my items and made me re-enter the store.

After checking my receipt, they quickly realized that I had, in fact, paid for everything. The manager later apologized, but by then the damage had been done. At that point, I asked them to refund my entire purchase because I no longer wanted to support a store that treated me this way.

While I waited for the refund, the employee who made the accusation avoided me and stood out of sight behind a refrigerated display. She refused to approach me, acknowledge her mistake, or offer an apology.

Based on how I was singled out and treated, I believe this incident was racially motivated and that I was profiled. I have continued shopping here despite a litany of previous poor customer-service experiences, and this incident was simply the icing on the cake. Every year I purchase turkeys from this location to help feed approximately 50 families from SMMUSD schools. However, I will not tolerate being falsely accused or racially profiled. This experience was humiliating, unacceptable, and deeply disappointing. I hope Vons will take this incident seriously, address what happened, and do better for everyone in the community.

docs.title: Review of Vons
docs.text:
Google review of Vons (5 out of 5, by Ta Conner, 2 months ago): Daniel and Ganae at Vons on Wilshire went ABOVE AND BEYOND for me!

I had less than 24 hours to get a custom cake with a photo on it and at least 6 different bakeries told me it was IMPOSSIBLE bc it required at least 48 hours notice. For some reason, I called Vons on Wilshire back for the second try and, this time, Daniel answered the phone. I explained to him that i DESPERATELY needed the cake for a very special occasion (a co-worker who is like a daughter was turning 22 and I overheard her trying to buy her own cake!). He told me not to worry, that he could get it done by 9AM the next morning! He walked me thru the ENTIRE process OVER THE PHONE (everyone else demanded i place the order thru the app, which made the turnaround time IMPOSSIBLE). He recommended a good size and shape for the cake and EVERYTHING down to the icing trim. I was literally in shock! He even gave me his cell # so I could reach out for updates. Who does that?!??!

Here's where I had to trust the process...He was leaving in 30 minutes (3:30 pm), the decorator wasnt there, but he assured me he would leave the precise details INCLUDING the urgent turnaround time for the decorator who would be in the following morning at 4 AM (and he would arrive at 7 AM). Mind u, I need this cake by 9!. So now im supposed to trust that another person is going ti get in board to make this whole thing happen???!?! YES!

Next morning, rolled at the bed ASAP and called VONS. The cake was already done and all Ganae had to do was write Happy Birthday on the side!!!!

When I arrived to pick up the cake, I almost fainted from how amazingly beautiful the cake was! Better than I expected! I hugged Daniel and Ganae so tight and couldn't stop thanking them enough. This was more than just getting a cake done, i really wanted to bless a young lady with a surprise for her birthday. And not just any surprise. She was literally trying to order her own cake! And when the other coworkers and I came out with the cake, the look in her eyes and the smile on her face was PRICELESS.

GOD BLESS DANIEL AND GANAE for their professionalism and expertise, but most of all, their EXTRA EFFORTS AND KINDNESS!

docs.text:
Google review of Whole Foods Market (1 out of 5, by FF53, 4 months ago): Could not disagree more with the “alleged” 5 star reviews. Our neighborhood store for years & have watched a steady decline in overall management & customer service. Partly blame Amazon culture since they bought it. Yes, cashiers are nice & it’s convenient to drop into such a small store & pick up a staple quickly. That aside, serious staffing concerns. Rather than write a public review, shared privately several with floor ‘“managers”, the latest, watching a guy at deli pop food in his mouth (no gloves) while chatting with a coworker in front of customers.  A young woman in deli screaming & carrying on like a hyena every single time there. Non service dogs everywhere.  Behaviors you do not see at Wilshire & San Vicente. Clearly a management/oversight issue.

We’ve moved onto the neighborhood Bristol Farms & we’re not the only ones.  Great customer service, never seen a dog period, amazing salad & hot food bar & above all great staffing & customer service with the same or better “natural” food choices as WF.

It offers a wide selection of fresh produce, meats, seafood, prepared foods, and specialty items that cater to health-conscious shoppers.

Google review of Pavilions (5 out of 5, by Theo Shayo REALTOR, 2 months ago): During our stay in Santa Monica, we found ourselves stopping by Pavilion’s several times to grab groceries, snacks, and a few essentials. The store was always clean, well-stocked, and easy to navigate, and the staff was friendly each time we visited.

One thing that stood out to us person traveling from Texans was the difference in alcohol laws. Back  in Texas, you can’t buy hard liquor at grocery stores or on Sundays, so it was definitely interesting to see spirits available right in the grocery store. It’s always fun noticing the little differences when traveling!

Overall, Pavilion’s was a convenient and reliable place to shop during our vacation, and we’d happily stop by again on our next visit.

Google review of Vons (1 out of 5, by Markeisha Haynes, 2 months ago): My profound disappointment regarding a recent experience at the hot food department. As a frequent patron of this  establishment, particularly due to its convenient location near my workplace, I have generally held this store in high regard, and my interactions with your staff have typically been positive. However, an incident on Saturday, August 8th, presented a stark contrast to my usual experience with the following employees : San Yon, and Steve

Upon approaching the hot food counter, I waited approximately three minutes while two employees were present. While I was initially engaged in selecting my meal and am accustomed to a brief wait for acknowledgment, the situation escalated when one employee, who was preparing sushi, addressed me in what was as an aggressive tone, and attitude stating, "You need to ring the bell in order for someone to come help you." This sudden and confrontational remark was both unexpected and unprofessional.

My subsequent request to speak with a department manager appeared to agitate this employee further. During my conversation with the manager, the same employee repeatedly interjected, exhibited a disrespectful demeanor, and continued to make unprofessional comments, thereby disrupting my attempt to convey my concerns privately and constructively.

Adding to this unfortunate situation, another employee, identified as Steve, emerged from the back of the store and interjected into my discussion with the manager. He directly contradicted my account of events, despite not having been present during the initial interaction at the counter. His unsolicited intervention further exacerbated the discomfort and unprofessionalism of the entire exchange.

The cumulative effect of these interactions has left me profoundly dissatisfied. The level of customer service I received on this occasion was entirely unacceptable and falls significantly short of the standards I would expect from any establishment. I will no longer be patronizing this  store. I believe that such experiences directly undermine customer loyalty and reflect poorly on Vons brand

Google review of Bay Cities Italian Deli & Bakery (5 out of 5, by JG, 7 months ago): Finally made it to LA’s ‘veteran of sandwich’ who’s been there even before tons of the newbies existed. I have been missing out for so long, not knowing they sold tons of other produces and imported quality stuffs! I felt like literally being able to spend long time just going through the alleys.

Great effort they did to make the wait time shorter, they premade some of their favorite menus so people needn’t wait as they’re ready to grab. Google review of Fromin's (5 out of 5, by Paul Mark Morris, a year ago): Fromin’s Deli in Santa Monica is easily one of the best delis in Los Angeles and without question the best on the West Side. The soups here are the star. The matzo ball soup is excellent with a rich, flavorful broth and dumplings that are light yet satisfying. The vegetable soup is another standout, full of fresh flavor and balance, and there are other soup options that keep the menu interesting.

The corned beef is a classic favorite, tender and perfectly prepared, and pairs well with their rye bread. Pastrami, brisket, and turkey are also consistently delicious and show the same attention to quality that runs throughout the menu. Fromin’s recently refreshed the space, which now feels brighter and more comfortable while still maintaining its identity as a real deli. It is not trying to be fine dining, and that authenticity is part of the appeal.

Service is always strong. The staff is quick, attentive, and friendly, keeping things moving while still being warm and welcoming. Plates arrive hot and fresh, and the overall pace adds to the feeling of being in a true neighborhood institution.

Fromin’s has everything you want in a deli: unbeatable soups, excellent sandwiches, reliable service, and a setting that feels both classic and updated. This is five stars all the way.

Google review of Bagel Nosh Deli (5 out of 5, by Zan Lee, 10 months ago): Stopped in for my first time today and I was really impressed. I thought it was just a bagel shop, but it is honestly more of a deli and bagel shop hybrid. Basically you order at the counter and being that I was there for breakfast I was surprised to see a lot of breakfast options like pancakes, but I especially liked how most of the dishes included a bagel with it, which is what I was there for initially. I was able to find free parking in their tiny lot in the back, otherwise it will be street parking. It was quite busy when I arrived, but our food came out surprisingly fast after ordering it, and the staff was very friendly.

Inside is quite large, there are many different size tables, no booths or counter seating, it is all regular sized tables. I did not see an outdoor eating area when I was there, everything was inside. For my breakfast, I chose an omelette, and with that it came with a bagel, so I decided to go with a cheddar jalapeño and really liked it. It was packed with jalapeños, and you can tell it was made that morning. The omelette was also a good sized portion and had great flavor. It’s not a full service restaurant in that they don’t have waiters tending to you, however, they will bring the food out to your table, and the staff that I encountered was very friendly and helpful. I would suggest to anyone and plan to be back again very soon.

Google review of McCall’s Meat & Fish Co. (3 out of 5, by Michael Smith, 8 months ago): McCall’s has a great selection and it’s always convenient to pop in for a bottle of wine or something quick for dinner. We’ve enjoyed shopping here over the years and appreciate having it in the neighborhood.

That said, it’s getting uncomfortable to be prompted for a tip on every single transaction — even when simply purchasing a bottle of wine at the counter. Being handed the payment device with an expectation to tip for a basic retail purchase feels misplaced and awkward.

Tipping has its place, but applying it to standard over-the-counter sales risks frustrating loyal customers. I hope management takes a thoughtful look at this approach, because many of us genuinely want to continue supporting the business without feeling pressured at checkout.

docs.text: Google review of Petitgrain Boulangerie (4 out of 5, by Thuong, 4 months ago): Really cute little shop, always a line out the door. The staff is extremely warm and welcoming. docs.title: Review of Petitgrain Boulangerie
docs.text: Google review of Petitgrain Boulangerie (5 out of 5, by Gabrielle Urman, 5 months ago): These are legit the best pastries in the country. I’m amazed with the perfection of each item. Seriously the best chocolate chip cookie and raisin rolls in existence. I personally LOVE the lemon pistachio croissant and the zaatar olive feta roll. Oh, and the oatmeal cookie of course! There can be long lines, but they usually move quick. The place itself is very small and they sell unique high quality local stuff aside from their pastries. There’s a bench outside for some seating, but I’d recommend taking it to go and enjoying in the car or at a park!

docs.title: Review of Petitgrain Boulangerie
docs.text:
Google review of Petitgrain Boulangerie (5 out of 5, by Mandy Grogg, a month ago): Would fly back for the cardamom swirl ✈️

One of, if not the best, cardamom anything pastry that we’ve tried in our adult lives together. This morning was very rainy so unsure if this is a common experience or not, but it was extremely sweet to have someone pass out hot tea and chocolate chip cookies while in line. The interior was cozy and didn’t have anywhere to sit (we missed that in the planning to stop here in the rain) so we took everything back to the car to include four pastries, coffee, and orange juice. I feel like everything we paid for was actually priced quite well and it was justified for the quality and product. We look forward to swinging by here again in a few weeks!

* croissant: would have again; loved the peach-passion fruit butter. get a thing of butter for sure!
* concha: strawberry matcha, loved but we were ready to move on after a few bites
* cardamom swirl: no notes; be thinking about this for weeks.

We were in LA to fly to Maui and made sure to stop by on our way home. We got a lot of stuff and spent $140 for 2 big bags full of goodies! We got the French toast sticks, breakfast grilled cheese, a variety of donuts and pastries, the tots/latkes, quiche, a loaf of brioche bread and I’m sure I’m forgetting something lol. docs.title: Review of Modern Bread and Bagel
docs.text:
Google review of Modern Bread and Bagel (3 out of 5, by R R, 7 months ago): It was my first time going to this location. I have been to the one in Beverly Hills before and liked that one more

We were the only customers and yet the cashier kept trying to ignore us which was super weird. Also their coffee machine and bathrooms weren't working... There was also a lot of stuff lying on their bar seating counter so it made it feel like we were not supposed to be there.

They had quiche just sitting out on the counter the whole time we were there.. this makes me nervous to order quiche from them again. I had ordered it before for delivery from the BH location and was fine, but seeing the folks at this location leave it out to get spoiled makes me concerned about the food safety.

I ordered the vegan bacon bagel sandwich that my friend from NYC had recommended to me, as him and his wife go to the NY location frequently. Mine unfortunately was tasty but a bit dry. Asked my friend later and he said oh it's because you have to get it with a runny egg. Interestingly the cashier had not asked how I wanted the egg cooked or made any advisement.

I don't like having to put a bad rating but I genuinely want them to do better. I understand the owners are expanding but that doesn't mean you should leave existing locations to such disappointing level of disarray

docs.title: Review of Randy's Donuts
docs.text:
Google review of Randy's Donuts (2 out of 5, by Kitty Kitty, 9 months ago): I grew up in Inglewood with the original Randy’s before it became really famous. Aside from the Inglewood location, I tried them at Resorts World in Las Vegas and they were amazing!! I was really excited to try the Santa Monica location but was disappointed. First, when we walked in the smell was off, not a sweet donut smell at all but a stale odor filled the air. Customer service was good, we were greeted by someone who walked in from the back, he nice.
We purchased a variety of donuts, about one dozen. All, and I do mean ALL of them had a stale/old frying oil taste. We tried to force it and eat them anyway because we know they’re good donuts but we just couldn’t. The texture was good, like these could’ve really been good donuts, the potential was there but they used old oil which unfortunately made them unappetizing. Maybe it was an off day, maybe the cook did something not normally done etc…. I do not know but what I do know is they messed up. These donuts are far to expensive and have to great of a legacy to be fried in old/stale oil. I recommend going to another location.

docs.title: Review of Randy's Donuts

We tried the Nutella donut and glaze twist. The Nutella donut was not sweet at all. Chocolatey for sure but very tolerable. Amazing. The glaze twist was on the sweeter side though. The staff were super super friendly. Totally recommend!

docs.title: Review of H&H Bagels
docs.text:
Google review of H&H Bagels (5 out of 5, by Zan Lee, 10 months ago): Stopped in for my first time today and overall had a great experience and delicious bagel. The ordering system here is a little bit clunky and disorganized. Also after we ordered the guy at the register disappeared so we pretty much stood there for 10 minutes while the line built up until someone had to come over and check us out, aside from that experience was nice. Parking can be a bit tricky, but we were able to find a metered street spot directly in front of the restaurant and opted to get everything to go, but they do have many tables inside to sit down and eat so dining in is an option. The menu is pretty large and they have all sorts of bagel shop classic options on there. The staff was friendly and aside from waiting to pay everything that we ordered was made very quickly.

For this visit, we chose the Lox bagel, the Avocado, Egg, & Cheese and the Bacon, Egg, & Cheese Bagel. We also tried the Blueberry Bagel with the Cookie Cream Cheese, and that was especially sweet and fantastic. All of the bagels we ordered were fresh and each of the three were very good and we would definitely order them again. Overall, it was a good experience and I plan to be back again in the near future.

docs.title: Review of H&H Bagels
docs.text:
Google review of H&H Bagels (3 out of 5, by Margaux, a year ago): I have never been to H&H Bagels in NY, so I cannot compare. But I did see about this place online and was super curious to try. I have been disappointed with some bagel places around here, and I have my specific spots that I like.

Anyway, so I wanted to try this one. I had already passed by it a few times and it was always crowded with long line.

So, we went on a weekend, it was crowded, but we probably waited 10-15min. It can still be considered as a lot, but I wanted to try.

Inside it gets a bit loud, and the way to order is not very easy as you have a big glass between you and the worker. You kind of have to yell to make yourself heard - imagine when you have to name a bunch of different ingredients.

After that, you go to the register to pay where you need to repeat your order again. I just feel it’s a bit messy as a system. And, then you need to find the person who took your order.

Now comes the time to try the food. The bagel is fairly big with quite a lot of food inside. But… it was a bit blend in terms of taste to be honest. I did ask for toasted bagels, but if they actually did it, it was very light so that was disappointing as well.

And, I don’t have much more to say - it was just a very basic bagel, so for me it didn’t live up to the hype.

I would try it again very well toasted with salted butter, and then it might bring me that NY vibe.

Google review of Sam's Bagels (2 out of 5, by Bianca G., 2 months ago): Update:  July 26, 2026
Sad to say I had a terrible experience this morning and will probably never be coming back.  I got there just before a second worker arrived for the morning at around 7:45 a.m. and the first one was totally stressed out.  He cut my bagel unevenly were one side was totally flat and thin and the other side was fat and thick.  This has been an ongoing issue.  I don't think anyone wants their bagel cut this way.  This morning this happened again.  I went back and showed the second guy that had just arrived the bagel and he offered to give me another one which I thought was wrong because this has happened so many times the minimum that he could do is give me a new Bagel cut properly and give me a one time credit for the inconvenience.  Instead the guy in the back the initial one came out started videotaping me with his phone, pointing at the cameras and yelling at me saying that I was complaining too much. I thought are you kidding me right now?  I was offended embarrassed because he did this in front of other customers and it was unjustified especially since they were in the wrong.  The guy that arrived later would not give me the owner or managers contact information to let them know about what had happened.  It really started my Sunday off wrong what should have been a calm Sunday and I could have sat and had my bagel and my coffee in peace.  It set me back time wise because I needed to get maintenance done on my car by a certain time and it disrupted a second meeting that I had for brunch with a family member which I had to cancel.  All because this guy took his stress out on me. I refuse to absorb the stress that he took out on me and move on with my day although he disrupted my schedule.  Things like this really do matter.  Sam this time you really got it wrong. Talk to your workers about treating customers with more respect.

Previous review:
Sam got it right! 👍

Google review of Élephante (5 out of 5, by pit & pon, 3 months ago): Absolutely loved this place! The atmosphere and vibes are amazing, making it a perfect spot for lunch or dinner. It does get super busy, so I definitely recommend making a reservation in advance.

The food was delicious from start to finish. My favorites were the Margherita Pizza, Calamari, Grilled White Shrimp and the Tagliatelle Tartufo, every dish was flavorful and well prepared. If you’re visiting for the first time, I highly recommend ordering those.

Great food, great energy and a beautiful setting. I can’t wait to come back!

docs.title: Review of Élephante
docs.text: Google review of Élephante (5 out of 5, by Elena, 2 months ago): This restaurant has a wonderful atmosphere. We had a pizza and salad it was delicious. And the cocktails also nice!! We visited here as a tourist and we was sitting at the bar. The bartenders are so friendly and kind. Thanks to them I got good memories. I’m sure I will visit again

docs.title: Review of Élephante
docs.text:
Google review of Élephante (5 out of 5, by Nate Ulsh, 4 months ago): Came for late lunch and it was a great meal, amicable staff and quick service. The entryway is a little funky to find the elevator but the view and ambiance is amazing once you get there. Parking garage across the street is really convenient.

The menu selection is a bit limited but food was very delicious. The ricotta pancakes were moist and fantastic, meatballs were cooked well and great. The arugula pasta has a gritty taste but overall good. Overall great experience.

docs.title: Review of Élephante
docs.text: Google review of Élephante (5 out of 5, by KaRee Copeland, 3 months ago): Élephante was absolutely perfect! The stunning view provided a wonderful setting for my daughter's birthday celebration. The phenomenal breeze truly enhanced the experience. Service is an art, and the staff demonstrated mastery in every aspect! From the hosts to the front of house, kitchen, and wait staff, all my needs were anticipated and met. Even a birthday surprise was handled with great care. Our brunch was phenomenal! I highly recommend ordering the pancakes and the calamari! P.S. Valentino, your service was perfect! Reservations are not required, but they are highly recommended.

docs.title: Review of Élephante
docs.text:
Google review of Élephante (5 out of 5, by Pono Guerrero, a month ago): Incredible Brunch Views and a Vibrant Late-Night Vibe!

Élephante is an absolutely fantastic spot for brunch in Santa Monica. The open terrace offers beautiful ocean views and a great breeze that make for a perfect morning setting. I ordered the Eggs Benedict, which was excellent and unique—it comes served on a crispy hash brown patty with avocado. It was incredibly satisfying and super filling!

The atmosphere completely shifts in the evening, and it becomes a major hotspot. I went back around 11:30 PM on a weekend hoping to grab a late-night order of their Cacio e Pepe, and the place was totally packed with great energy. A huge bonus for this spot is that their kitchen actually stays open until 1:30 AM! I originally planned to wait for the crowd to thin out a bit, but I ended up getting too tired and calling it a night before ordering.
I’ll definitely be back for that Cacio e Pepe next time.

I highly recommend checking this place out, whether you want a relaxed, scenic brunch or a lively night out!

docs.title: Review of Din Tai Fung
docs.text:
Google review of Din Tai Fung (5 out of 5, by DM TANG, 3 months ago): Ooh, wow! What a pleasant surprise!

Not that I hadn’t already heard plenty of compliments about Din Tai Fung, especially this Santa Monica location, but I was still surprised by how uniquely beautiful it is.

We were a group of six and were lucky enough to be seated 15 minutes before our reservation. Our table was right by the window next to the outdoor patio, overlooking the Pacific Ocean and just steps away from the fire pit. It was after sundown and a bit chilly, so sitting by the fire pit with the overhead heaters made the entire dining experience extra cozy.

The food was delicious, just as expected. My soup dumplings arrived piping hot, which, to me, is always a good sign of freshness and authenticity. We also tried the chocolate xiaolongbao out of curiosity, and it did not disappoint. My kids especially loved the sea salt cream with a touch of matcha.

Our server, along with everyone who helped clear dishes throughout the meal, was incredibly warm and helpful. He happily took photos for our group and introduced several dishes, making us feel well taken care of.

This restaurant made our celebration of my daughter’s 19th birthday even more memorable. We highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys delicious food, warm service, and spectacular ocean views—especially after sunset.

docs.title: Review of Din Tai Fung
docs.text:
Google review of Din Tai Fung (5 out of 5, by Uğur Bulduk, a month ago): Absolutely loved our experience at Din Tai Fung! The dumplings were especially delicious — fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. The restaurant has a beautiful atmosphere and everything felt well organized and welcoming.

Definitely a must-visit if you love dumplings. Highly recommended! 🥟

docs.title: Review of Din Tai Fung
docs.text:
Google review of Din Tai Fung (5 out of 5, by Chartreux, 2 months ago): Really enjoyed Din Tai Fung in Santa Monica! 🥟

The soup dumplings were delicious — thin skin, lots of flavorful broth, and perfectly cooked. The shrimp fried rice and shrimp wontons were also very good. The quality was just as good as what I’ve had in Taiwan.

The service was friendly, and the location is super convenient, right in Santa Monica Place. Great place to grab a meal before walking around the mall or heading down to the beach.

Definitely recommend it, and I’ll be back next time I’m in Santa Monica!

docs.title: Review of Din Tai Fung
docs.text:
Google review of Din Tai Fung (5 out of 5, by Afshin Shoja, 3 months ago): Din Tai Fung in Santa Monica completely lives up to the hype! Located right in the upper level of shopping mall, it’s incredibly convenient to get to, especially since you can just park in the attached parking structure without any of the usual beach-side parking headaches.
The restaurant itself is stunning. The indoor-outdoor patio setup is gorgeous, featuring a bright, modern design with artificial turf accents and sleek circular seating that makes the whole dining experience feel upscale yet relaxed. Plus, you get some fantastic views of the surrounding area right from your table.
As for the food, every single dish was a hit:
Xiao Long Bao (Soup Dumplings): Absolutely flawless, packed with flavor and perfectly delicate.
Spicy Wontons & Noodles: The sauce has just the right amount of kick and pairs perfectly with the vibrant green noodles.
Garlic Green Beans & Wood Ear Mushrooms: The green beans were perfectly crisp and garlic-forward, and the wood ear mushrooms added a wonderful, refreshing crunch to the meal.
Drinks: Pairing everything with a chilled bottle of Nigori sake made the meal even better.
The service was prompt and attentive, keeping up with the busy mall crowd seamlessly and beach. 🏖️

docs.title: Review of Din Tai Fung
docs.text:
Google review of Din Tai Fung (5 out of 5, by Scott Lee, 3 months ago): Din Tai Fung is a very nice restaurant with a clean and comfortable feeling. I really liked the outdoor seating area. It had a chill and relaxing vibe, and they also have heaters above the table area, which helps keep your head warm when sitting outside. Nice little detail.

The food was good, and I especially liked the cucumber appetizer. It was fresh, flavorful, and a great starter. The portions are a little smaller and the price is higher, but that is kind of expected for Din Tai Fung, especially inside a mall.

One small tip: the restroom is located at the back of the restaurant. If you see a red light above the door, that means it is being used.

Overall, great food, nice outdoor setup, and a very comfortable dining experience.

docs.title: Review of La La Land
docs.text: Google review of La La Land (5 out of 5, by Marian Grant, 8 months ago): I was looking for a good cooler on a warm winter day here  in Santa Monica. This cafe hit the spot. Don’t let the long line fool you. The service is fast. You can also order ahead via the website or app. There is cozy seating in the front of the cafe as well to the back of the cafe. There is also comfy seating outside side. The bright yellow decor is inviting. This is an awesome place to work on your laptop. I ordered a mango passion fruit cooler. Not overly sweet! You can pick up your order inside as well as the outside walk up window. The cafe and the patio area is kept clean. Parking can be a challenge due to limited street parking.

docs.title: Review of La La Land
docs.text:
Google review of La La Land (3 out of 5, by Alison Carter, 5 months ago): Did a mobile order. Pickup was confusing. Apparently mobile orders are meant to be picked up from a window outside, but I saw no signs or instructions with my mobile order indicating so. Staff acted like I was stupid for not knowing this.

One of my drinks was not yet ready when I came, and when I asked an employee about it, he asked for my name, then walked away and never made my drink. Another server did, but only after filling several other orders first. Okay?

docs.title: Review of La La Land
docs.text: Google review of La La Land (5 out of 5, by Renny Engbring, 9 months ago): If you want VIBES LaLa Land is your destination. But they don’t sacrifice quality for vibes, which is key. Coming mid week in the morning is the best time, because the line is not too long. The line can be out the door, which at the end of the day is a good sign. Matcha 10/10, even just your standard iced Matcha latte. They have so many fun options though too, in a selection of cream tops - vanilla, banana, or their matcha squared (matcha with matcha cream top). The attention the detail here is pretty incredible and it’s so cutesey. I mean, heart shaped straws? Come on. Great merch available too. The staff is so friendly! Bring your computer and get to work or bring a friend for a date. Oh, and the pastries look unbelievable 🤤

docs.title: Review of Cobi's
docs.text:
Google review of Cobi's (5 out of 5, by Montira Clippard, 5 months ago): 🍛🥘🌶️ A Hidden Garden in Los Angeles Serving Southeast Asian Flavors Worth Celebrating

My friends brought me to Cobi’s to celebrate my birthday, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve had in Los Angeles.

From the moment we walked in, it felt like stepping into a hidden oasis. Tucked behind lush greenery and twinkling lights, the space has the charm of a secret garden—cozy, intimate, and incredibly inviting.

🌶️ Flavorful Southeast Asian-Inspired Dishes

What surprised me most was how vibrant and flavorful every dish was.

* Bold Southeast Asian flavors with layers of spice, citrus, and herbs
* Beautifully presented plates that were ideal for sharing
* Creative combinations that felt exciting yet balanced

Each dish brought something unique to the table, making the meal feel like a culinary journey.

🌿 Atmosphere & Design

The ambiance alone makes this place worth visiting.

* Romantic garden setting with lush plants and warm lighting
* Cozy but energetic atmosphere
* Perfect for birthdays, date nights, and special celebrations

It feels like one of those places you discover and immediately want to tell your friends about.

👏 Service

The service was warm, attentive, and helped make the birthday celebration feel even more special.

⚠️ Good to Know

* Reservations are highly recommended
* Best enjoyed family-style so you can sample a variety of dishes

Cobi’s offers more than just a meal—it creates an experience. Between the beautiful setting, flavorful dishes, and thoughtful service, it was the perfect place to celebrate.🎉😋

docs.title: Review of Cobi's
docs.text: Google review of Cobi's (5 out of 5, by Brilliant Hua, 4 months ago): My husband and I hosted an intimate wedding dinner at Cobi’s and I could not recommend it enough. I was blown away by my experience start to finish. Even before the dinner, the event host, Camila and the manager, Aaron were so professional and communicative. On the day of, the service was fantastic, the room was beautiful, and the food was delicious. I’d recommend Cobi’s to anyone wanting to host a special event, date night, brunch or family dinner. Apart from their events, we’ve come for both brunch and dinner so I know it’s consistently great.

docs.title: Review of Cobi's
docs.text:
Google review of Cobi's (5 out of 5, by Len, 4 months ago): Everything about this place felt right.  From the hostess, to the flowering 💐 decore before going into the restaurant, to the vibe, to the interior warm decor, and the workers.  The positive energy was evident, and you can feel and see it amongst not only the workers who seem content, but also the patrons.

Don't get me wrong, but the food was the star ✨️ of the show.  The crispy rice salad 🥗 was amazing!  I want to re-create this dish, but I'm sure it won't come close to how I experienced it.  Definitely a must-order when we go back to So-Cal (NorCal person represent! Side-note, our server was wearing a 49ers 🏈 Tee, and he admitted a friend gave it to him.  He joked that he's a bandwagon with pride & a smile. I respect that!  He said he doesn't want to be associated with a losing team, and we laughed!  I agree).

Getting back to the restaurant review, let's continue to keep the vibe pf how good the food is.  We asked for his recommendations, and we happily obliged tp order the fried chicken and the roti wraps.  The fried chicken 🍗 was crispy, seasoned perfectly, and paired well with everything we ordered.  I wish we ordered steamed rice 🍚 to go with it, because in my upbringing, that's what we did.....eat steamed rice with every protein, lol!  Luckily, we had crispy rice salad that allowed me to indulge the chicken with.

The roti wraps were so good, and filling.   We had one of each, and I enjoyed both of them instead there own ways.  I would have both styles again.

Great job to everyone who is involved with this restaurant.  I hope you continue to do great things!

docs.title: Review of Sweet Maple
docs.text:
Google review of Sweet Maple (5 out of 5, by Ronnie S., 2 months ago): ​⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ An Unforgettable Morning at Sweet Maple
​If you are looking for the absolute gold standard of breakfast, Sweet Maple is in a league of its own. From the moment you walk through the doors, the timeless, welcoming ambiance sets the perfect mood—warm, vibrant, and classic without trying too hard.
​The menu is packed with hits, but a few standouts make this place an absolute must-visit:
​The Blackstone Benedict: Perfectly poached eggs and rich, velvety hollandaise layered over savory bacon and sliced tomatoes. Every single bite is pure perfection.
​The French Toast: Decadent, golden, and melt-in-your-mouth tender. It hits the exact right balance of sweet and indulgent without feeling overly heavy.
​The beverage game here is just as strong:
​Bloody Marys: Bold, perfectly spiced, and served with just the right kick to kick off the morning.
​Cappuccinos: Expertly crafted with rich espresso and silky, smooth foam—a coffee lover’s dream.
​Beyond the incredible food and drink, the service was top-tier. The staff was warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming from start to finish, ensuring everything arrived fresh and fast despite a busy dining room.
​Sweet Maple effortlessly balances incredible food with a warm, timeless atmosphere. 5 out of 5 stars—we will be back again and again!

docs.title: Review of Sweet Maple
docs.text: Google review of Sweet Maple (5 out of 5, by David Beesley, 6 months ago): I would like to start off with saying by far one of the best experiences and food I have ever had in a restaurant setting. Realistically, it was some of the best food I’ve had in my life. The atmosphere and the server were phenomenal. I would genuinely recommend anyone traveling to this area or from this area to take advantage of the opportunity to dine in this exquisite place. The eggs in my omelette were super fluffy and perfectly seasoned. No condiments or sauces needed. The potatoes were perfect consistency with a variety of potato and refreshingly also did not need anything added to it. The burger was so juice and full of flavor. As a picky ranch eater, their ranch is to die for. Unfortunately I did not get to try their signature bacon they are known for but I’m sure it’s just as great as everything else there. I’m so bummed that I live in Utah and have to think about this place all the time and can’t just go there again. I’ll say this place is a must for anyone looking for a great environment to spend time with family, friends, loved ones and also be treated would be upmost respect and service if I could give this place a rating it would be 100 out of 10. I will be sure to go back there at the first opportunity I have!

docs.text:
Google review of LouLou Santa Monica (2 out of 5, by Vanessa Pastrano, 5 months ago): My birthday experience at Loulou Rooftop Restaurant & Lounge (brunch) honestly wasn’t one of the best.

The place has a very cute and fun atmosphere with Tulum vibes, and that energy definitely matches the decor. The vibe and aesthetics are probably the best part of the place.

However, my rating mainly comes down to the food, because it should match the overall experience they’re trying to offer. The menu is basically Mediterranean food that feels very basic, lacking flavor and nothing extraordinary for a brunch spot that’s supposed to stand out.

Even worse, the cocktails were terrible. We tried an Old Fashioned that tasted mostly like water, and the Palomas were way too sour. After that, we decided not to order more drinks because we didn’t want to keep getting disappointed.

As for the service, it wasn’t bad, but it definitely wasn’t outstanding either. We basically saw our waitress about three times.

Honestly, the price does not justify the experience. I would recommend it for the vibe and pictures, but if you’re looking for great food, drinks, and an overall memorable dining experience, I wouldn’t recommend it.

docs.title: Review of LouLou Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of LouLou Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Jeremy Hayz, 4 months ago): Had the pleasure of dining at LouLou Rooftop Restaurant & Lounge in Santa Monica and really enjoyed the experience. The space is absolutely beautiful with a fun Tulum-inspired vibe. I can only imagine how stunning it becomes later in the evening when the sun goes down and all the lights come on, it seems like the kind of place that completely transforms at night.

What stood out most was the teamwork among the staff. Everyone was helping each other, which created such a welcoming atmosphere. Our server, Sophie, was an absolute sweetheart. She took her time explaining menu items, answered all of our questions, and delivered genuinely professional service throughout the meal.

As someone who loves trying a little bit of everything, we ordered quite a few dishes. I always joke that a bigger table is better because I tend to order enough food for four people, even when dining for two! The team quickly accommodated us by bringing another table over, which was appreciated. The Caesar salad was flavorful, generously dressed, and far from dry. The Hamachi Crudo was incredibly fresh and one of my favorite dishes of the evening. The escargot was delicious as well, though slightly overcooked for my taste. We also tried two pizzas, the dough was excellent with a great texture and flavor, although I would have loved to see a few more topping options. Even with there toppings it was not well placed all the mushrooms were on 1 slice and the meat was scattered (not evenly made).

Overall, a very enjoyable dining experience with great food, beautiful surroundings, and wonderful hospitality. Looking forward to coming back and experiencing the rooftop after dark.

docs.title: Review of The Cheesecake Factory
docs.text:
Google review of The Cheesecake Factory (5 out of 5, by Mariana Moraes, 4 months ago): I’ve been going to The Cheesecake Factory for years, even before I moved to the United States. It’s actually one of the places I always take friends and family when they come visit because I feel like it gives such a fun “American dining experience.” Their menu is huge, with so many options for every taste, which makes it perfect for groups.

This time, we went to celebrate my husband’s birthday, and as always, the food was delicious. We ordered from the SkinnyLicious menu because we wanted lighter options, and I honestly love that they offer meals that are less caloric without sacrificing flavor. Everything I’ve had there over the years has always been consistently tasty.

I also really love the atmosphere. Every location has the same signature look and feel, and I think the restaurants are beautifully decorated, warm colors, elegant details, and a very welcoming environment. It feels polished and comforting at the same time.

And of course, the cheesecakes are amazing. I’ve tried many flavors over the years, and not a single one disappointed me. They truly live up to the hype.

The only reason I’m giving 4 stars instead of 5 for service is because of a small disappointment during this visit. Since it was my husband’s birthday, we thought he would receive a complimentary cheesecake slice, which had always been part of our past experiences there. Our waiter wasn’t very clear that this had changed, and in the end, we were charged for it. Later, I found out that now you need to be part of the Rewards program to receive the birthday cheesecake. If I had known, I definitely would have signed up beforehand to continue the tradition.

Even with that, we still had a great experience overall, and it continues to be one of my favorite classic American restaurants

docs.text:
Google review of The Cheesecake Factory (5 out of 5, by Tommy Ramsey, 7 months ago): Santa Monica Nights, Cold Air, Warm Moments

We kicked off an early Saint Patrick’s Day this past weekend out in Santa Monica, and I’m not going to lie, it was one of those nights you just sit back and appreciate.
The place was packed. Energy everywhere. People out celebrating, music in the air, just a good vibe all around. It felt like the whole city showed up.
Now the only thing that tried to ruin it was that cold fog rolling in off the water. It hit hard. One minute you’re good, next minute you’re freezing. That ocean air doesn’t play around.

But even that couldn’t touch the night we were having.

My wife and I ended up at The Cheesecake Factory, and that’s where everything just settled in right. We were told it would be about a 40 minute wait for a table, but honestly, we didn’t even care. We grabbed seats at the bar instead.

Best decision we could have made.

We were already in celebration mode, so sitting at the bar just fit the moment. Drinks flowing, appetizers coming out, no rush, no pressure. Just us enjoying the night.

And the food hit. Exactly how it’s supposed to.

The Cheesecake Factory doesn’t miss when it comes to variety and consistency. The appetizers came out hot, flavorful, and right on time. No drop in quality, even with how packed it was. That says a lot.
What stood out even more was how welcoming everything felt. Even though we switched things up and stayed at the bar, there was no attitude, no disconnect. We were taken care of the whole time.
By the time our table was ready, we were already done eating. And you know what? That was perfectly fine. We didn’t need it. We already had the experience.

But let’s be real.

The best part of the night had nothing to do with the crowd, the drinks, or even the food.

It was being there with my wife.

Talking, laughing, just locked into each other with everything else going on around us. She makes everything better. Every place feels different when she’s there. More real. More complete.
That’s what I’ll remember.
Not the wait. Not the fog.
Just us.
And nights like that, you don’t take for granted.

Google review of Water Grill (5 out of 5, by Kyan Bartel, 3 months ago): We had an absolutely fantastic date night at Water Grill in Santa Monica! The entire experience felt upscale, lively, and incredibly memorable.

We started the evening with some of their cocktails, which were exceptionally tasty, unique, and beautifully crafted. For appetizers, we shared a sushi roll and the grilled octopus. The octopus was the absolute star of the start of our meal—perfectly charred and completely fantastic!

For entrees, the cioppino was amazing. It was rich, incredibly flavorful, and packed to the brim with all sorts of delicious, fresh seafood. I originally had my heart set on the Chilean sea bass, but since they were completely out of it for the night, I opted for the lobster roll instead. It turned out to be a blessing in disguise because it was absolutely delicious and packed with tender meat.

The atmosphere has beautiful views of the water and a great, energetic vibe. While the ambiance was a bit on the louder side, it didn't detract at all from the beautiful setting and great energy. To top it all off, the service was good and highly knowledgeable; our server gave us great insights into the menu.

We will definitely be back for another date night soon!

Google review of Water Grill (5 out of 5, by Nikki T, 2 months ago): Traveling for work allows me the opportunity to try lots of restaurants.  Some of my co-workers and I ventured to Water Grill for dinner after a long day of being in a conference room.  We made the short walk to Water Grill for some seafood.

We started with chilled wild jumbo Mexican shrimp.  I also ordered a ½ pound of chilled mussels.  We also split a salad.  For my main I ordered the wild Ross Sea Chilean sea bass with butternut squash gnocchi and sage brown butter.  Two of my friends got the tagarashi seared bigeye tuna.  They said it was rather spicy probably since tagarashi means “seven flavor chili pepper.”  My other friend also ordered the sea bass but she got the gluten-free version which came with grilled vegetables.  We were too full to get dessert.  I know...shocking because I love dessert.  But fret not....I came back for Round 2 the next day.

Yes, I came back the next day for lunch after a serious power walk on the beach.   This time I came in for a late lunch and sat up at the bar.  I ordered the chilled mussels again, a bowl of the claim chowder and the jumbo lump crab cake.  I was hungry!  I also ordered the key lime pie to go.  The New England-style chowder was topped with a few little neck clams.  The crab cake had a little spicy kick to it but it wasn’t overpowering. It was a lot of crab meat and not a lot of filler, just the way I like it.  I had the key lime pie later and it had the right amount of tartness one expects in a key lime pie with a huge amount of meringue topping.

If you’re in the mood for seafood, I recommend Water Grill.  It also has a patio so you can enjoy the California coast line and the Pacifica Ocean.

Hillstone continues to set the standard for consistency, quality, and outstanding hospitality. From the moment we arrived, everything was polished, welcoming, and professionally executed.

We started with the perfectly prepared Cobb salad, which was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully balanced. It made for an excellent beginning to the meal. For our entrées, I ordered the 8-ounce filet mignon cooked medium-rare, and it was absolutely flawless—tender, juicy, and cooked precisely to temperature. We also enjoyed the baby back ribs, which were outstanding. The meat was incredibly tender, falling effortlessly off the bone, with a rich, smoky flavor and a perfectly caramelized glaze that made them unforgettable.

What truly elevated our experience was our phenomenal server, Michael. His extensive knowledge of the menu, attention to detail, and genuine enthusiasm for the restaurant were impressive. He offered excellent recommendations, answered every question with confidence, and ensured that every aspect of our dining experience was seamless and enjoyable.

The combination of exceptional food, impeccable service, and Hillstone's refined yet comfortable atmosphere made for a memorable evening. Every dish was executed with precision, and the level of hospitality was second to none.

Hillstone remains one of Santa Monica's premier dining destinations, and after this experience, it's easy to understand why. We look forward to returning soon.

Highly recommended and well deserving of five stars. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Google review of UOVO Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Andrea Harlan, a month ago): Such a great find just off Third Street Promenade!

My family and I were walking around Third Street Promenade and were in the mood for really good Italian food. We heard about UOVO, walked one block over to Second Street, and I’m so glad we did.

One of the things that makes it so special is that all of the pasta is handmade in Italy using Italian ingredients and flown overnight to the restaurant every day.

We ordered the yellowtail carpaccio, lasagna, carbonara, and tonnarelli with pomodoro sauce. Everything was delicious, and everyone loved it, including the kids. We were enjoying the food so much that I forgot to take pictures of the pasta, but I did manage to snap one of the yellowtail!

The staff was friendly and attentive. UOVO is also a no-tipping restaurant. A 16% service charge is automatically added to the bill and they do not accept additional tips. Since we normally tip 20%, that was perfectly fine with us.

Really delicious food and such a fun family dinner.

Google review of UOVO Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Edwin, 9 months ago): Hands down, this is the best pasta bar I’ve tried. Everything looks simple at first glance, but every dish is cooked to order and absolutely perfect. Watching the chef work the open kitchen is part of the fun, you can really see the care and precision that goes into each plate.

The cacio e pepe was unreal. Finished in the cheese wheel, with the melted cheese clinging perfectly to the pasta, rich, creamy, and so satisfying. The ragu looked pretty humble, but once it was tossed with that perfectly al dente pasta, the depth really came through. You could taste how long that meat sauce had been slowly cooked down, deep, savory, and full of flavor.

Such an awesome lunch spot overall, and I’ll definitely be back for more.

Google review of Shake Shack Santa Monica (4 out of 5, by Did You Z That!, 8 months ago): Me and my wife stopped here on a day-trip to Santa Monica, we were starving and having tried Shake Shack in the past but in Florida, we gave here a try.
I’m glad we did.

The food:
I went for the Double SmokeStack with fries and a tiramisu shake.
My wife had a VegeStack with cheese fries and a coffee shake.

The food was really nice and you can tell was made fresh, with the burger being juicey and fries being hot and freshly made. The milkshakes were equally good, especially the tiramisu, highly recommend it.

The service;
The server was nice enough and food arrived promptly, no complaints.

Atmosphere;
It wasn’t bad, pretty quiet and enough where you can talk with the person/s you’re with.

OVERALL:
It was around $52 for everything mentioned above which you could say the price is around the same you’d probably pay for Five Guys. The food was very good, however I do feel that the Florida Shake Shack was better which the burger was juicy enough that I didn’t need sauce. Whereas this one, I felt like I needed to dip the burger in sauce to get the full flavour and soak up the patties.

Props for Shake Shack suppling free water and on demand too.

Google review of Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. (4 out of 5, by Misha Smith, 7 months ago): I’ve been to several Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. locations over the years, including the one in Los Angeles and one in Colorado, and I’ve always had friendly experiences.

During this visit, I was especially delighted that we were able to be seated even though our entire group hadn’t arrived yet. We had a hard time finding parking, but thankfully it all worked out in the end. Since we were a large group, service took a little longer than we anticipated, which we completely understood.

Our server, Dean, was very friendly and attentive, which made the experience pleasant. Unfortunately, the food wasn’t quite as great as I remembered, and my dish was extremely spicy. Dean kindly took it off the bill and made sure I received something that worked better for me, and I didn’t have to pay the difference. I truly appreciated that level of customer care.

All of the staff were super friendly, and the restaurant — including the restrooms — was very clean. I also want to mention how kind they were in accommodating our mom, who was having difficulty with the stairs. They opened the gates for her, which meant a lot to us.

Thank you for making it a memorable experience.

docs.title: Review of Bubba Gump Shrimp Co.
docs.text:
Google review of Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. (5 out of 5, by Travel Maker, 6 months ago): Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. Santa Monica is one of those places where the view and atmosphere make the experience even better than the food.

Honestly, this was one of the most memorable meals during my Santa Monica visit. Sitting by the window with a view of the ocean and the pier just hits different, especially around sunset.

The shrimp dishes are what you expect — tasty and satisfying — but the real highlight is the whole experience. The Forrest Gump theme, the casual vibe, and the location right on the pier make it feel special.

It’s definitely a bit touristy and not the cheapest option, but you’re paying for the location and atmosphere.

✔ Amazing ocean view (especially at sunset)
✔ Fun Forrest Gump themed restaurant
✔ Great spot for a relaxed meal
✔ Perfect Santa Monica experience

If you’re visiting Santa Monica Pier, this place is worth stopping by at least once.

docs.title: Review of Meat On Ocean
docs.text:
Google review of Meat On Ocean (5 out of 5, by Urgamal Azat, 5 months ago): We ended up at Meat on Ocean thanks to the enthusiasm of the hostess team, and they set expectations high from the start. Luckily, the experience matched the hype.

The atmosphere struck a great balance, lively but still comfortable. Our server, Kirby, was wonderful, friendly, attentive, and made sure everything flowed smoothly throughout the meal.

We went with the center cut tenderloin served with mushrooms and asparagus, and it did not disappoint. The steak was perfectly cooked and full of flavor, and even the fries were a standout, crispy and hard to stop eating.

Overall, a really enjoyable dining experience that we would happily repeat.

docs.title: Review of Meat On Ocean
docs.text:
Google review of Meat On Ocean (1 out of 5, by Jimmy Lu, 2 months ago): Came here for the Dine LA menu at $75 per person and was pretty disappointed with the experience.

The pricing was very misleading. The ribeye was an extra $10 and the Wagyu ribeye was an extra $25, but the additional charges were written in very small text underneath the dishes, basically the same size as the sauce and other option descriptions. The way it was presented made it look more like an optional add on or side charge rather than an extra charge for choosing that steak. It was really easy to miss, and no one mentioned the extra charges when we ordered. For a set menu, this should have been made much clearer.

The food was also disappointing. There was grit and sand in the salad, and the shrimp had a really strong fishy smell and did not taste fresh. The steak was extremely undercooked. The center was basically raw and the meat was very difficult to chew.

The chocolate cake also had a noticeable refrigerator taste, like it had been sitting in the fridge for a while.

Our final bill for four people ended up being over $500. For that price, the quality of the food and the overall experience were nowhere near what we expected. Completely not worth the money and we definitely would not come back.

docs.title: Review of Meat On Ocean
docs.text:
Google review of Meat On Ocean (5 out of 5, by Kay, 5 months ago): I had the most amazing bread I’ve ever eaten .. honestly enough to make me want to come sit at the bar just for cocktails and bread alone. We had the wagyu flight and the 60-day dry-aged steak, and every single bite was unbelievable. The quality, presentation, and attention to detail throughout the entire meal made it feel like such a special dining experience.

The ambience was warm, upscale, and inviting without feeling pretentious, and the service from Valentina was absolutely phenomenal. She was knowledgeable, attentive, and made us feel genuinely taken care of from start to finish. It’s rare to find a place where the food, atmosphere, and service all exceed expectations, but this absolutely did. Already looking forward to my next visit.

docs.title: Review of Meat On Ocean
docs.text: Google review of Meat On Ocean (5 out of 5, by BongNosher, a month ago): Dinner at Meat On Ocean really delivered on every front. The dry-aged steak came out pre-sliced and smothered in melting herb butter, packing an incredible crust and that deep, concentrated richness you only get from serious aging. The seafood held its own just as well—the Chilean sea bass had a gorgeous golden sear with huge, buttery flakes over braised red cabbage, while the salmon nailed that elusive combination of paper-crisp skin and a juicy, flaky center. Even the lamb chops were a standout, perfectly charred on the outside with a tender, smoky pink bite paired with wild mushrooms. Paired with grilled asparagus, cheesy roasted cauliflower, and a warm, caramel-drenched bread pudding with melting vanilla ice cream to wrap things up, it was easily one of those meals where practically every dish was a hit.

docs.title: Review of Meat On Ocean
docs.text:
Google review of Meat On Ocean (5 out of 5, by Erik Suwandy, 2 months ago): I came here to celebrate my niece/nephew’s and my dad’s birthdays, and we had a really enjoyable experience.

Justin was an amazing server. He explained the menu in detail and gave us some great recommendations that we were very happy with. The atmosphere was also wonderful, especially with the beautiful view overlooking Santa Monica Beach.

We ordered several dishes:

• Clam Chowder Bowl – Savory, rich, and creamy. The soup had a nice thick consistency and was very flavorful.

• Wagyu Gold Filet Mignon, 6 oz & 8 oz – My parents felt these were a little too salty. It seemed like there may have been a bit too much sea salt sprinkled on top.

• 45-Day Dry-Aged T-Bone & 45-Day Dry-Aged Porterhouse – These were definitely my favorites! Both steaks were juicy, tender, and cooked beautifully. The portion sizes were also very generous and satisfying.

• Mashed Potatoes – A perfect side for the steaks. The flavor was mild and not too heavy, so it balanced the richness of the meat really well.

• Asparagus – Nicely tender and savory.

• Sautéed Mushrooms – Another favorite of mine. They were aromatic, flavorful, and had a great texture.

Overall, I really enjoyed this steakhouse. The food was delicious, the service was excellent, and the oceanfront atmosphere made our birthday celebration even more special. I would definitely come back!

docs.title: Review of Mel's Drive-in
docs.text:
Google review of Mel's Drive-in (4 out of 5, by Gee Angelo, 3 months ago): We chose Mel’s Drive-In for our last dinner in America, and it was a great way to end an unforgettable Route 66 trip.

The food was exactly what you hope for from a classic American diner. Huge portions, freshly cooked, full of flavour, and great value. We enjoyed everything from the burgers and chicken to the desserts, which were absolutely delicious and the perfect finish to the meal.

A special thank you to our server, Olive, who was warm, friendly and attentive throughout. She really made us feel welcome and looked after us brilliantly.

The only reason I’m giving 4 stars instead of 5 is that another member of staff who helped us later seemed a little impatient. We were a larger group and needed a bit of extra time to decide what we wanted, but we felt a little rushed.

Aside from that, we had a lovely evening. Great atmosphere, generous portions, tasty food, and a fitting final meal before heading home. We’d happily visit again.

docs.title: Review of Mel's Drive-in
docs.text:
Google review of Mel's Drive-in (5 out of 5, by Shae B., 4 months ago): Came across this place by accident and I’m glad I did.

Atmosphere:
It’s the cutest little diner. Every table has a jukebox and we were too excited to drop a quarter and play all our favorite oldies.

Service:
There was no wait to be seated. Our server was so nice and attentive. I think her name is Olivia. She took our order and our food was delivered fairly quickly.

Food:
My daughter ordered the Smash Burger with fries and an Arnold Palmer.  I ordered the Mels Patty Melt with fries and a Mimosa. Everything was delicious! We didn’t have room for dessert but we stayed parked on the lot and walked around the city. By the time we returned we’d worked up an appetite for dessert.
We ordered the Strawberry Shortcake and Butterfinger Milkshake to go(couldn’t get a picture of the shake my daughter couldn’t put it down). The Strawberry Shortcake was Scrumptious! I can’t wait to come back! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Google review of Mel's Drive-in (5 out of 5, by Mercy R, 5 months ago): What a beautiful back to the past this restaurant is so nicely kept up.
Loved my club sandwich, I read a review about how good this is, and decided to give it a try, and didn’t disappoint.

Google review of Mel's Drive-in (5 out of 5, by David Rincon, 6 months ago): Mel’s Drive-In on Lincoln Blvd is one of our favorite spots, and we visit often. docs.title: Review of HiHo Cheeseburger | Santa Monica
docs.text: Google review of HiHo Cheeseburger | Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Bobby W, 2 months ago): Heard about HiHo’s Wagyu ingredient and wanted to check out their burgers. After our hike in the Santa Monica Mountains we paid them a visit. We ordered “Pastrami Heat” burgers double wagyu patties with the addition of pastrami and spiced onions. Heat was just perfect with the burgers nicely done. The pastrami is fantastic. Blushing soft pink. Gorgeous. We ordered a Ceasar Salad and Fries with the “Matty Sauce” was nice with a touch of spice. Is it Marie Rose with addition of some sriracha? Milkshakes are thick and delicious. Anyways. We enjoyed it so much a couple of days later we went back for the same again.

docs.title: Review of HiHo Cheeseburger | Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of HiHo Cheeseburger | Santa Monica (4 out of 5, by Nick O, 4 months ago): A great, low-stress addition to the Santa Monica burger scene. The primary selling point here is the sheer convenience—you get a quality meal without having to endure the agonizingly long lines that usually plague the area's top-tier burger joints.

The burgers themselves are undeniably good and hit the spot, but they don't necessarily reinvent the wheel. It’s a completely solid, reliable option if you happen to be in the neighborhood and want a quick, satisfying bite, but it’s probably not the kind of destination you need to cross town or go completely out of your way for.

If you're nearby and looking for a straightforward, no-hassle meal, it absolutely does the job. Well done HiHo Cheeseburger!

Google review of HiHo Cheeseburger | Santa Monica (3 out of 5, by E M, 6 months ago): The fries were absolutely incredible—crispy, flavorful, and definitely the highlight of the meal. Unfortunately, the burger itself was disappointing, as the meat was not cooked nearly enough, which was especially concerning for me as I am pregnant.

I also found the prices to be relatively high considering the portion sizes. That said, I want to note that the staff were very kind and welcoming, which we really appreciated. Overall, a mixed experience with great service but some important issues with the food.

Meat was cooked perfectly and tasted great. Well garnished. Well dressed. Great balance. Oh and those spicy onions were an amazing addition!Genius! Burger perfection.
