docs.title: Review of North Italia
docs.text:
Google review of North Italia (5 out of 5, by Владислава Франц, 2 months ago): Overall, we had a good experience. The atmosphere was wonderful, the restaurant was very clean, and the food was delicious.
I’m giving 4 stars because my husband’s pasta was extremely spicy, even though there was no indication on the menu that it would be spicy. We checked the menu and asked our server, who explained that the chef had added chili flakes to the dish. As a result, my husband couldn’t eat it. We appreciated that the restaurant handled the situation professionally and removed the dish from our bill.
It would be helpful if spicy ingredients were clearly indicated on the menu or if guests were informed in advance.

docs.title: Review of North Italia
docs.text:
Google review of North Italia (5 out of 5, by Bül Ent, a month ago): We had a wonderful lunch at North Italia in Santa Monica and left full and very happy.

I ordered the Crushed Meatball Ragu, which was flavorful, rich and absolutely delicious. I also had the meatballs as an appetizer, and they were excellent. Our son has celiac disease, so eating safely is extremely important to us. The restaurant was able to prepare gluten-free penne with Bolognese sauce for him, and he really enjoyed it.

My wife ordered the Little Gem Caesar with chicken, which was also very good. The chicken was initially missing, and my appetizer arrived a little later than expected, but both issues were handled quickly and professionally. Small mistakes can happen, and the attentive way the staff resolved them gave us no reason to take away a star.

We especially appreciated that the team appeared knowledgeable about gluten-free requirements and took our son’s needs seriously. Based on our experience, North Italia is a very good option for guests with celiac disease. Of course, anyone with celiac disease should always speak directly with the staff and confirm the current preparation procedures, as menus and kitchen practices can change.

The restaurant has a stylish and welcoming atmosphere, the service is attentive and professional, and the location is fantastic—just a short walk from the beach. We left the restaurant completely satisfied and happily headed back toward the ocean.

Delicious food, a great atmosphere and very considerate service. A well-deserved five stars!

docs.title: Review of North Italia
docs.text:
Google review of North Italia (3 out of 5, by Zeinab Elreichouni, 5 months ago): The vibes were great and the servers were helpful and easy to talk to. We got quite a few dishes. I personally tried the Margherita pizza, the sea bass, the calamari, and the arincini. The apps were good, flavored well and came with several dipping options! My negative is with the pizza. It may just be that I wasn’t expecting it, but the crust was a bit thicker than typical margherita pizzas from Italian restaurants. It also lacked basil.

My family got two of the pastas, they enjoyed them but expressed it could use some additional salt and seasonings.

I wouldn’t consider the pricing outrageous, but it is by no means affordable and I think based on that, the portion sizes (pastas were a bit small), and the taste of the food, I’m ultimately giving it a 3/5.

docs.title: Review of North Italia
docs.text:
Google review of North Italia (5 out of 5, by Monique Quiros, 8 months ago): Last-minute dinner on a Friday night of a holiday weekend, fully expected a long wait and chaos. Instead: no wait, smooth seating, and genuinely great service. Already winning.

We ordered the calamari to start (perfectly crisp, not greasy), split a pizza that was solid and satisfying, and I had a pasta with a white sauce that was rich, comforting, and exactly what I wanted. Everything came out hot, well-paced, and clearly made with care.

For a spontaneous plan on one of the busiest nights of the weekend, this was an easy, enjoyable dinner. Consistent food, attentive service, and zero stress. Would absolutely come back, especially knowing they can handle a crowd without dropping the ball.

docs.title: Review of North Italia
docs.text: Google review of North Italia (5 out of 5, by M. Gaspar, 4 months ago): This is a great place to go just after the beach as it’s such a short walk away. Everything here is always excellent! The fig and prosciutto pizza and fontina polenta are amazing. The highlight of our night was our server Evelyn who went above and beyond giving us recommendations, checking in on us, and taking special care communicating with the kitchen about my partner’s gluten allergy. Will definitely be back soon, thanks Evelyn!

docs.title: Review of Jack in the Box
docs.text:
Google review of Jack in the Box (5 out of 5, by john jewell, 7 months ago): Here you go, John — SoCal flavor, first-person, smooth and real:

---

I stopped by the Jack in the Box on Santa Monica Blvd and honestly, this spot delivered.

I ordered the Hot Mess combo and it came out hot and fresh, no lag, no attitude — just solid service. The sandwich was stacked with those crispy jalapeño onion rings and that creamy white sauce that cools the heat just enough so you can actually taste everything. Perfect balance. Crunch, spice, creamy smoothness — all working together.

They didn’t skimp either. The curly fries were generous and seasoned just right. You know that moment when fries are fresh out the fryer and still snapping a little? That. Plus two tacos on the side — classic Jack tacos, always dependable — and an ice-cold Coke to seal the deal.

For Santa Monica prices, this felt like a real bargain. Hot, tasty, filling, and fast. The crew was cool and professional, and the food came out exactly how you want it — fresh and dialed in.

Sometimes you just want something satisfying without the whole production, and this place hit that SoCal comfort vibe perfectly.

I’ll definitely swing back through.

---

Both were super fresh, flavorful, and had a nice level of heat without being overwhelming. The texture and quality really stood out, especially for a quick-service sushi spot.

docs.text:
Google review of ROLLD Sushi (5 out of 5, by dawn cheng, 4 months ago): Convenient little cute sushi roll shop on the westside. Newly opened by a couple from Australia, Rolld Sushi is able to maintain quality and freshness by keeping their menu simple. The menu rotates daily, consisting of 5 or 6 classic rolls (salmon, tuna, yellowtail, and vegetarian options as well). The interior is modern, clean, and there is ample natural lighting - making for a very airy feel. There is no seating inside, although there are cute little seats outside to eat your rolls and people watch. Service is quick - you just point to the rolls you want, and the friendly staff package your selections. The rolls come with cute fish-shaped soy sauce bottles, wasabi, and ginger. There is decent street parking in this area of Santa Monica.

docs.text:
Google review of Urth Caffe Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Aparna Tiwari (The wandering foodie), 4 months ago): This place is combo of all, n no of coffee/tea options , bakery and dessert have some decent no of option but very unique one, they food menu too is very huge serving good breakfast, sandwiches , flat bread and so on.. the food was just so fresh and breads too were very nice.
Tried their coffee and rumi latte.. those to were good.
Located at corner of road with a comforting ambience.

docs.title: Review of Urth Caffe Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of Urth Caffe Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Mariana Moraes, 4 months ago): I went to Urth Caffé for the first time and had such a great experience. It was pretty busy, but surprisingly easy to get a table since people are constantly coming and going.

I went for brunch with a friend and we both really enjoyed it. The menu is huge with so many options, it was honestly hard to choose. I ended up getting a breakfast sandwich, which was delicious and very generous in size (I couldn’t even finish it).

The ordering process is simple: you order at the counter, get a number, and they bring the food to your table. The staff was super efficient, the servers and busers were working quickly and keeping everything moving smoothly.

It’s a perfect spot if you’re walking around Main Street or even if you just came from the gym and want something satisfying. I highly recommend it and will definitely be coming back!

docs.title: Review of Urth Caffe Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of Urth Caffe Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Katrina, 4 months ago): They have a large menu with plenty of options to choose from, but I was surprised by how limited the vegetarian and vegan offerings were.
The restaurant gets very busy, so be prepared for a wait, especially during peak hours. I ordered the avocado toast with egg and a smoothie, and both were delicious. The portions were also much larger than I expected, which was a nice surprise.
Parking was easy to find, with plenty of street and metered parking available, as well as several nearby parking lots. Overall, I enjoyed my meal and would definitely come back, though I wish there were more vegetarian and vegan options on the menu.

docs.title: Review of Urth Caffe Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of Urth Caffe Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Tricia A. Edward, 4 months ago): As someone visiting Santa Monica on my very first trip to California, Urth Caffé was exactly the kind of experience I was hoping to find. From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere felt vibrant, welcoming, and uniquely California.

I ordered the salmon lox on buckwheat bread, the avocado toast, and a honey latte—and every bite was incredible. The salmon was fresh and flavorful, the avocado toast was piled high with fresh greens and perfectly ripe avocado, and the honey latte was smooth, comforting, and easily one of the best coffee drinks I’ve had.

What made it even more memorable was enjoying such fresh, wholesome food while soaking in the laid-back Santa Monica vibe. It felt like the perfect California breakfast/brunch experience. If you’re visiting the area, especially for the first time, Urth Caffé is absolutely worth a stop.

A highlight of my trip and a place I’ll be thinking about long after I leave California!

docs.title: Review of Urth Caffe Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of Urth Caffe Santa Monica (4 out of 5, by Alex G, 4 months ago): Delicious pastries! I tried the Nutella Girella bun and the Napoleon creme and both were excellent. The pastries tasted fresh and were made with high-quality ingredients with generous portion sizes that made them even more enjoyable.

The place has a vibrant beachside atmosphere with both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a great spot to relax and enjoy a treat.

Parking can be a bit difficult to find but it's manageable. I added a photo of the parking restrictions most spaces have a 2-hour limit which wasn't too bad for a visit.

docs.title: Review of Tartine Santa Monica
docs.text: Google review of Tartine Santa Monica (4 out of 5, by Andrea M Dinh, 2 months ago): Cute little gem with a really fresh, chic sitting area  loved the atmosphere. I had the salmon tartine and my husband the tres leches. The smoked salmon tartine was the star  the lemon notes and spices hit just right, really yummy. The coffee was decent and the tres leches cake was good,  not very sweet. Wouldn’t go out of my way to come back but if I’m in the Santa Monica area, I’d definitely stop in again.

docs.title: Review of Tartine Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of Tartine Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Jacky Lam, 6 months ago): Absolutely amazing experience at Tartine Santa Monica. From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere feels warm, stylish, and inviting. The pastries are next-level — perfectly flaky, rich, and not overly sweet. The bread is clearly made with incredible care and craftsmanship, and you can really taste the quality in every bite.

I especially loved the morning bun and the country loaf — both were outstanding. The coffee was also excellent and paired perfectly with the food. Staff were friendly, efficient, and made the whole experience even better.

It’s definitely a spot worth going out of your way for. Easily a 5-star bakery and one of the best in the area. Highly recommend!

docs.title: Review of Tartine Santa Monica
docs.text: Google review of Tartine Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Joe Skokan, 4 months ago): Nice place! Warm out so we sat outside. Food was very good. Spendy, but this is Monica. For example, there was a slice of chocolate cake, a slice, like less than an inch thick, for $6.50. To compare a coffee shop in my home town of Seattle called Herkimer sells similar for $4.00.

docs.title: Review of Tartine Santa Monica
docs.text: Google review of Tartine Santa Monica (3 out of 5, by Outta Townies, 5 months ago): Tartine Santa Monica is a beautiful cafe surrounded by other cute places. Looks like it used to be an old church. Lots of seating inside and out. Had to wait in a line but it went pretty fast and we were able to checkout all the amazing fresh baked goods while we waited. The staff and service wasn’t great. They were not welcoming or friendly. They were having a conversation while I stood there. I finally said hello and they acted like I was interrupting their break. The food and coffee were very good! I ordered a latte, the farmers bowl, and a brownie! So tasty and fresh! I even tried recreating it home and it just was not the same. Prices were a little high. Overall, you should check it out if you are in the area, just know you might have to wait, it’s expensive, and the staff might be rude.

docs.title: Review of Tartine Santa Monica
docs.text: Google review of Tartine Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Brandon Nolte, 6 months ago): Came here to celebrate my mother-in-law’s birthday. While this place is known for its bread, the real surprise was the burger. It was incredibly juicy, tender, and perfectly seasoned, with a house-made sauce that elevated the whole dish. I have no idea what was in it, but it worked. I would absolutely order it again.

docs.title: Review of goodboybob Coffee Roasters
docs.text:
Google review of goodboybob Coffee Roasters (4 out of 5, by R D, 5 months ago): I come to Goodboybob at least once a week and overall I really enjoy it. The coffee is consistently great, the location is super convenient, and lately I’ve been really into the brown butter latte.

What prompted me to write this review is the pistachio cake. It was decent, but I was honestly surprised when I realized it was $12 for a single slice. I didn’t catch the price until it was already being rung up, and that felt pretty steep for what it was. I personally wouldn’t pay $12 for it again.

The frosting was also very sweet. I think it could really benefit from a bit of salt to balance out the buttercream. That said, everything else about the shop is solid and I’ll definitely keep coming back for the coffee.

docs.title: Review of goodboybob Coffee Roasters
docs.text: Google review of goodboybob Coffee Roasters (5 out of 5, by Angelina Diamond, 6 months ago): Love this little hidden coffee house. Fantastic latte coffee! Enjoyed a delicious bacon egg avocado wrap aka Nueske, an amazing orange cranberry scone. The outdoor seating area is perfect for sipping and conversation. Went back again before leaving.

docs.title: Review of goodboybob Coffee Roasters
docs.text: Google review of goodboybob Coffee Roasters (5 out of 5, by Lisa Nussdorfer, 2 months ago): I was staying in Santa Monica and met a friend here.  It was hidden away, but the vibe was cool and the espresso was perfect.  I bought a bag of coffee. I randomly picked the Ascent Blend and it was perfect when it was brewed at home.  I actually could taste the citrus.  Not pictured was the burrito I got.  So…I was by far the oldest one there but I still got the cool vibe.

docs.title: Review of goodboybob Coffee Roasters
docs.text: Google review of goodboybob Coffee Roasters (5 out of 5, by KaRee Copeland, 6 months ago): Good Boy Bob, should be on your list in Santa Monica. A quaint location but with stellar service. I tried a signature drink BBL😉 and I was not disappointed! The pastries are homemade and the burritos, to die for!!! Try THE SIX!!!!!! The staff is friendly and knowledgeable about their business. I am forever loyal!

docs.title: Review of goodboybob Coffee Roasters
docs.text:
Google review of goodboybob Coffee Roasters (3 out of 5, by Corey Z, 2 months ago): You approach the counter after waiting in the sun for 10 minutes. A light fan dissuades bugs from consuming the appealing pastries to your left. A sign advertising a creamed espresso brings you to reconsider your usual cortado. A brief thought skitters across your consciousness, a brief whisper that you’ve learned to ignore in this scenario…

How much does that drink cost?

You consider purchasing a bag of freshly roasted beans, noticing no price is listed amidst the selection.

You glance at some unremarkable fruit in a bowl under the iPad register.

$3.

Hmm… must be some single origin fruit?

You purchase that bag of beans; the lowest option costs $20. You take it home and realize you spent at least $10 less than required to make a properly tasty cup of artisanal pour over.

The evidence builds until you can’t ignore it any longer.

Goodboy Bob is overpriced.

docs.title: Review of Starbucks Coffee Company
docs.text:
Google review of Starbucks Coffee Company (4 out of 5, by Ian the Reviewer, 5 months ago): This Starbucks does a solid job handling what is clearly a very busy weekend crowd. The line moved surprisingly fast, and the staff stayed efficient and friendly even with constant foot traffic coming in from the promenade area. Service definitely deserves credit for keeping things flowing.

The atmosphere here has a darker, richer vibe compared to some brighter suburban Starbucks locations, which actually fit the area nicely. There’s seating for roughly 20 inside and another dozen or so outside, making it a decent place to sit for a while if you can grab a table. One cool touch is being within earshot of local street performers, which adds a fun and very “Santa Monica” type of energy to the experience.

The biggest downside was the restroom situation. There was a pretty serious bathroom line during my visit, and it seemed like the facilities just can’t fully keep up with the heavy weekend promenade traffic. To be fair, not everyone waiting appeared to be paying customers, so that probably adds to the challenge.

Overall, a good Starbucks location with strong service, a lively atmosphere, and a great people-watching spot.

docs.title: Review of Starbucks Coffee Company
docs.text: Google review of Starbucks Coffee Company (1 out of 5, by Eliska Janikova, 5 months ago): The order was completely wrong – I received something different than what I asked for. On top of that, the matcha latte was poorly prepared, not mixed properly, and full of clumps. The place also felt dirty. Overall, it felt very careless and rushed. This definitely didn’t deserve a tip.

docs.title: Review of Starbucks Coffee Company
docs.text: Google review of Starbucks Coffee Company (4 out of 5, by Catherine Cruz, a year ago): Beautiful Starbucks. Well located on 3rd Street Promenade, I just thought pretty strange that they don’t have any tables inside, today was very wind and I would love to sit inside drinking my coffee. It is a huge place with a lot of empty space inside. The service went fast and they were nice.

docs.title: Review of Starbucks Coffee Company
docs.text:
Google review of Starbucks Coffee Company (1 out of 5, by Jasira Intelligence, 8 months ago): Never before have I been racially profiled... sadly while I was at this store, I was told that I looked like the people who crashed the planes on 9/11.  Given the fact that this day was an excruciating painful memory (for us all) - you can imagine how offensive this was. I had on the hunter denim swag pant -it gives fashionista, it gives ready to dance.... it does not give how I was treated and the words I was called.

This was so next level you guys - that while every other customer received hearts and smiles on their cups, I received attitude from the barista - who literally threw Cinnamon at me after the whole ordeal -(male, tall, Hispanic, though I forgot his name). All that cinnamon literally thrown... like ... why? ...so much force used, missed the cup, and landed cinnamon all over the counter. I refused the drink.

Not sure exactly what this was -but it was shocking to see and far below the standard that Starbucks ever served.

I reported all this to Adriana and Kat and based on the airplane comment, they immediately sided, were rude and unprofessional. They saw me as "them" not as Us. It didn't matter how I was treated - all that mattered was HOW I LOOKED.

That aside, Rosa was the star. She was kind, apologized on behalf of her store managers and insisted that I contact the District Manager, Ryan. I spoke to Him today and am creating awareness so that this does not happen to anyone else.

*I captured a few pics highlighting the cinnamon, which unfortunately reflects the level of service received.

If I could rate this store a 0, I would.

docs.title: Review of Starbucks Coffee Company
docs.text: Google review of Starbucks Coffee Company (5 out of 5, by Anita Fish, 8 months ago): I've got to say, the screen showing the order queue is a total game-changer. No more awkwardly waving at the barista—I can just see exactly what's happening! Now, if only every Starbucks could get this magical screen, we’d be living in a coffee utopia.

docs.title: Review of Perry's Café & Beach Rentals - Santa Monica 2400
docs.text: Google review of Perry's Café & Beach Rentals - Santa Monica 2400 (5 out of 5, by Laurel Montella, a month ago): Everything I get to LA I head to Perri's in Santa Monica. The atmosphere is very chill, beach food & beer. You can watch beach volleyball or just relax and watch a Cali sunset

docs.title: Review of Perry's Café & Beach Rentals - Santa Monica 2400
docs.text:
Google review of Perry's Café & Beach Rentals - Santa Monica 2400 (5 out of 5, by Manny Steel, 2 months ago): Perry’s Beach Cafe is one of my favorite spots by the beach. The customer service is outstanding, and the staff is always welcoming, friendly, and attentive. Their iced vanilla coffee is excellent, perfectly balanced, refreshing, and consistently delicious.
The menu has a wonderful selection with something for everyone, whether you’re looking for a quick coffee or a bite to eat. The atmosphere is what really makes this place special. It has an amazing beach vibe that is relaxing, clean, and perfect for enjoying the ocean. If you’re looking for great coffee, excellent service, and a laid back coastal experience, I highly recommend Perry’s Beach Cafe.

docs.title: Review of Perry's Café & Beach Rentals - Santa Monica 2400
docs.text:
Google review of Perry's Café & Beach Rentals - Santa Monica 2400 (5 out of 5, by Hayley Di Naso, a year ago): Perfect spot for a beach beer! And love music on Wednesday & Friday in the summer!

We soaked up some sunshine and sipped on cold beers after a walk to the beach. The umbrella covered seating made it a great place to relax.

We didn’t eat but the food looked fresh and they had a nice selection on their menu. Something for everyone for sure!

Update: as we have been back multiple times since my original post. We’ve tried the good and so far the burrito was our favorite.

Also love that they have an additional bar and live music during the summer months on Wednesday and Friday. The musician was really good and added to the fun of the evening.

docs.title: Review of Perry's Café & Beach Rentals - Santa Monica 2400
docs.text: Google review of Perry's Café & Beach Rentals - Santa Monica 2400 (5 out of 5, by Ben Currie, 2 months ago): Coming from Canada and not having beach attire (towels, chairs, umbrellas, etc), we decided to use Perry's Rentals. So happy that we did! Booking was easy and so was check-in. Daily parking was affordable and right next to the cabana and beach. We were fortunate to have Lestyn as our "beach butler" as he was amazing! 5+ Star service for sure! Ordering our food and drink was extremely simple and both were quality as well. Our visit to Santa Monica and our day at the beach exceeded our expectations! Thanks to Lestyn and the rest of the team at Perry's Rentals!

docs.title: Review of Perry's Café & Beach Rentals - Santa Monica 2400
docs.text: Google review of Perry's Café & Beach Rentals - Santa Monica 2400 (4 out of 5, by Amelia Hughes, 3 months ago): Perrys was a great spot to stop for a frozen pina colada and strawberry margarita! We were able to enjoy the view of the beach, catch a bit of the world cup game, and sip on our drinks under the shade of a large umbrella! Didn't get to try the food this time around but we will be back on our next walk down the beach! Also a  great spot to watch the volleyball games on the beach!

docs.title: Review of Espresso Cielo
docs.text:
Google review of Espresso Cielo (5 out of 5, by Sophie Nowak, 10 months ago): Espresso Cielo was the perfect little coffee stop after our beach day, and I’m already thinking about when we can go back. We walked over from the pier and loved the cozy, relaxed vibe the moment we walked in. It feels like a true neighborhood spot – warm, inviting, and not overly “chain” or corporate.

I ordered a matcha latte and it was so good – smooth, not too sweet, and you could actually taste the matcha instead of it being buried in sugar or milk. It was one of those drinks you slow down to enjoy instead of just chugging on the go. We also got a cortado and loved it so much that after we finished, he immediately wanted to go back for round two and ordered a cappuccino. That alone says a lot. The espresso tasted rich and balanced, not bitter or burnt, and the milk was textured really well.

The staff was kind and efficient, and even though they were busy, the vibe stayed calm and comfortable. It’s the kind of place you could grab a quick drink or sit for a while and people-watch. Overall, Espresso Cielo is exactly what you want in a local coffee shop: great drinks, warm atmosphere, and the kind of quality that makes you wish it was in your own neighborhood.

It has a strong reputation for using well-sourced beans and delivering consistently well-balanced espresso-based beverages.

The coffee is the main highlight, with lattes, cappuccinos, and pour-overs that are smooth, rich, and thoughtfully prepared. The attention to detail in preparation sets it apart from typical chain cafés.

The atmosphere is modern, calm, and stylish, making it a great place to work, read, or meet someone casually. The space feels intentionally designed for comfort without being overly crowded or noisy.

Service is usually friendly and efficient, with staff who are knowledgeable about the menu and coffee options.

Overall, Primo Passo Coffee Co offers a premium, craft-focused coffee experience with a strong emphasis on quality, simplicity, and atmosphere.

docs.text: Google review of Blue Bottle Coffee (1 out of 5, by Georgi Slatko, 4 months ago): Please explain your policy on order processing and preparation. I came to pick up an order I’d placed via Dordash, and I was told to wait 3–5 minutes. Okay, I went outside and waited about 7 minutes, but since the café has clear windows, I saw that two other customers had come in after me, paid for their orders, and sat down to wait.  I went inside, thinking my order was ready and I could pick it up, but I was told to wait a couple more minutes. I thought, "Fine." Then I saw the barista preparing three drinks. I thought they were for me, but no—they were for the customer who came in after me, and then another drink for the next person who arrived after me.   I should note that they paid for their order at the restaurant, not online. I asked, “How is that possible?” and was told, “Well, you’ll just have to wait a little longer.” My order was four lattes. The first customer who came in after me had three lattes. I just wasted 17 minutes for nothing—that’s very unprofessional. Please follow the order of requests when processing them.

docs.title: Review of Capital One Café
docs.text:
Google review of Capital One Café (2 out of 5, by Elsie “MsParkerazzi” Parker, 2 months ago): I stopped by the Santa Monica Capital One Café because I was in the area and needed somewhere to sit and work on schoolwork.

I sat down at one of the bar-style work tables along the windows, took out my laptop, and attempted to plug it in. The first outlet did not work, so I tried a second. That one did not work either, so I tried a third.

At that point, a staff member who was nearby volunteered the information that it was not just those particular outlets. He pointed along the entire electrical/USB strip built into the table and told me that none of the outlets on that strip work. He then pointed to the other bar-style work table, also equipped with built-in electrical and USB outlets, and told me that none of those work either.

So apparently the Santa Monica Capital One Café has two dedicated work tables lined with electrical and USB outlets, and staff are fully aware that not one of them works.

What made the interaction even stranger was that the employee repeatedly pointed me toward the reservable meeting rooms and office spaces instead. I actually asked, “Are you serious? None of them work?” He confirmed again that they did not and once again referred me to reserving a room.

I told him that no one should have to reserve a meeting room simply to plug in a laptop and do some work. He said he understood, but again referred me to the reservable rooms and then suggested I speak with the manager.

And yes, I told him how ghetto I thought that was. This is a Capital One Café in Santa Monica. You mean to tell me that an entire Capital One café/bank cannot manage to keep the electrical outlets installed specifically at its work tables functional? Even the Downtown Los Angeles Capital One Café has working outlets.

I cannot say whether leaving all of these outlets nonfunctional is actually intentional. However, when staff already know that every outlet across both public work tables is unusable and the repeated response is to direct customers toward reserving a room rather than mentioning repair, maintenance, or even an anticipated fix, it certainly creates that impression.

Those outlets were obviously installed at those tables so people could plug in laptops, phones, and other devices while using the café. Customers should not need to reserve an office or meeting room to access basic electrical power when outlets are literally built into the public workspaces.

If the outlets are broken, repair them. If there is some other reason they have all been allowed to remain unusable, Capital One should explain it. But maintaining two entire work tables with nonfunctional electrical and USB strips while redirecting customers to reservable rooms is backwards and unnecessarily restrictive.

A café promoted as a place where people can sit, connect, and work should make sure the amenities designed for exactly that purpose actually work.

docs.title: Review of Kavahana
docs.text:
Google review of Kavahana (4 out of 5, by Shubham Kamdi, 9 months ago): As a total newcomer to the world of kava, I wasn't sure what to expect beyond "earthy tea." Walking into Kavahana, I realized quickly that this isn't just a drink—it’s a ritual.

Kavahana manages to feel both upscale and incredibly grounded. Unlike the high-energy, loud environment of a typical bar, the energy here is mellow and conversational. It’s the perfect spot if you’re looking to "socialize without the booze."

I tried their traditional kava, and the sensation is unique. The taste is definitely "root-forward" and earthy, but the immediate numbing of the lips and tongue was the coolest part. Within about ten minutes, a gentle wave of relaxation hit—my shoulders dropped, and my mind felt clear but calm. It’s a "clean" kind of chill that doesn't leave you feeling foggy.

The girl at the counter said no the guy behind her said yes.  Ordered 1 dark mocha latte large hot and 1 white chocolate latte large hot.  I was the only person there, 10 minutes later I  called up for 2 small iced coffees. I said are those iced I ordered hot.  The girl got mad that she made them wrong.  Same girl that took the order.  I then watched her pour those drinks into hot cups straining off the ice and added a little bit of hot coffe to make it appear remade.  I get my name called and my coffe slammed down on the counter, coffee shot out the lid, cause they were mad they made the drink wrong. docs.title: Review of Shoop's Delicatessen
docs.text:
Google review of Shoop's Delicatessen (5 out of 5, by Zan Lee, 8 months ago): One of the most consistently good breakfast spots in Santa Monica. Don’t think of it as a traditional deli, it is more so a breakfast and lunch spot that has a very large and diverse menu. One thing I love about this place is they have a lot of indoor and outdoor seating so whatever you’re in the mood for you’ll be able to get. Parking is also extremely easy, there is a giant pay lot directly behind the restaurant or you can look for metered street parking. Our waiter was extremely polite and everything that we ordered came out shortly after ordering it.

Inside is pretty large, larger than it looks from the street, so they can host many different sized groups. For this visit, I ordered one of their most famous dishes, which is the Pancakes with Bacon inside it. As you would guess they were very good and filling, and I would order them again. They have a lot of great options on the menu so it’s easy to get something new each time. I would suggest if you are in the area.

docs.title: Review of Shoop's Delicatessen
docs.text:
Google review of Shoop's Delicatessen (4 out of 5, by Zulema Oregel, 5 months ago): Not sure if the food is great because I just came to buy cheese (I had come to eat at the Urth across the street). The owner seemed really nice. Parmessan cheese was a bit pricey but I know that authentic Italian cheese tends to be so I dont mind. I still paid just under $20 for a 1lbs cheese slice. They have an assortment of other cheeses, including meats (they have imported Italian prosciutto) among other little things like teenie tiny Nutellas. ☺️ 🤏🏻

I do hope to return for some of their sandwiches.

docs.title: Review of Shoop's Delicatessen
docs.text: Google review of Shoop's Delicatessen (4 out of 5, by Robert Prescott, 3 months ago): So good.  We had the bacon pancakes and they were everything that people say!  Fluffy cakes and crispy maple bacon cooked in.  So delicious. Service was fast and friendly and we sat down right away.  Plenty of paid parking close by. There were so many great options on the menu I wish I could've tried.

docs.title: Review of Amai coffee
docs.text: Google review of Amai coffee (5 out of 5, by Maryam, 7 months ago): This is a fantastic café with very high-quality matcha. The drinks are authentic and taste just like what you would find in Japan. The desserts are also excellent and beautifully prepared. The ambience is calm, elegant, and very inviting, and the customer service is wonderful. It truly feels like you are enjoying a café experience in Japan with the same level of quality and attention to detail. I highly recommend this place for anyone who loves authentic Japanese matcha and desserts.

docs.title: Review of Amai coffee
docs.text: Google review of Amai coffee (5 out of 5, by Gabrielle Urman, 4 months ago): Wow the mango sticky matcha is out of this world. The perfectly balanced syrup pairs so well with their matcha and whole milk. It’s definitely on the sweeter side and not very matcha forward, but it’s sooo good!!! An incredibly well balanced sweet treat drink and very nice baristas!

docs.title: Review of Amai coffee
docs.text:
Google review of Amai coffee (5 out of 5, by Chris Sung, 6 months ago): First time visiting Amis Coffee right in front of Santa Monica College’s main campus. The shop is small but very clean and well-maintained, which I really liked.

I ordered the Banana Cream Matcha Latte, and it was surprisingly delicious—smooth, lightly sweet, and very refreshing. It’s a unique combination that actually works really well.

The price was $8 for one drink, which is a bit on the higher side, but the quality and taste made it worth it. I’d definitely come back again to try other drinks.

docs.text: Google review of Caffe Luxxe - Santa Monica (4 out of 5, by Joella r, 4 months ago): Nice coffee shop with tasty coffee. Barista (coffee connoisseur)with New York attitude. Love it.So if you’re home sick for little morning attitude rush, go to this location.

docs.title: Review of Caffe Luxxe - Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of Caffe Luxxe - Santa Monica (4 out of 5, by Carlo N., a year ago): Caffe Luxxe is an exquisite cafe and L.A.'s premiere coffee roaster. They're located in Montana ave in Santa Monica. They serve good coffee and tea drinks as well as pastries.

I have drove by them a few time and finally got the chance to check-in today.
I arrived early Sunday morning to grab a hot Caffe Latte and a Choco Croissant. Both items were good, however, I wish my croissant was warm. Service was spot on. Prices were a bit pricey but expected for the area.

Indoor and outdoor seats were spacious. Atmosphere was relaxing. Staff were competent and professional. Street Parking only.

Overall, it's modest coffee shop.

docs.title: Review of Caffe Luxxe - Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of Caffe Luxxe - Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Sharon, 2 months ago): My go-to coffee shop when I’m in LA! I adore it so much and they are always so friendly and talkative. This location has beautiful skylights and parking is so easy to find. The cappuccinos are AMAZING and perfectly frothed like Mugatu says.

You also can’t go wrong with any of their seasonal drinks, they are always flavorful and just enough sweetness. Oh, and their roasted coffee is divine (my fav is the pink one, but can’t remember the name right now). I saw they were acquired late last year and hope that everything stays the same and they take care of their current staff who are stellar. Love you Luxxe!

docs.title: Review of Caffe Luxxe - Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of Caffe Luxxe - Santa Monica (2 out of 5, by Ikhsan P, 2 months ago): I was a fan of this place until my last visit when I was served premade matcha. It honestly killed the joy for me 😭

I always looked forward to coming here, spending a few hours, and enjoying your matcha because I really love it. But the pre made matcha at my last visit just wasn’t the same. Your matcha is so good, so why make it ahead of time? It really lost its spark.

Please don’t do this! I genuinely love this place and want to keep coming back. Freshly made matcha is part of what makes this place special!

docs.title: Review of Starbucks Coffee Company
docs.text:
Google review of Starbucks Coffee Company (2 out of 5, by Markeisha Haynes, 4 months ago): Dear Starbucks Management,

I am writing to formally address an experience I had at your Santa Monica, California location  Lincoln & Pico on June 2, 2026. During my visit, I presented two sealed bags of Starbucks coffee beans with the intention of utilizing your complimentary grinding service.

Upon interaction with a team member, identified as Justin (or Justice), I was informed that he was unable to process my request. The reason provided was an alleged policy stating that coffee beans, even if sealed, could not be ground if they had been purchased from a different Starbucks establishment. This policy directly contradicts information I have received previously, which indicated that any sealed Starbucks coffee beans are eligible for grinding at any of your store locations.

Beyond the conflicting policy guidance, the barista's overall demeanor and communication style were notably unaccommodating and unprofessional during our exchange. Such conduct significantly detracts from the positive and welcoming atmosphere one typically associates with the Starbucks brand.

Exceptional customer service is a fundamental element in building and maintaining customer loyalty. Incidents like this not only create confusion regarding your service offerings but also negatively impact the customer's perception and willingness to return. Consequently, this particular experience has unfortunately made me hesitant to revisit this specific location, and has prompted a reconsideration of my future patronage.

I trust that this feedback will be valuable for your internal review of both customer service protocols and the consistent application of store policies regarding bean grinding.

Sincerely,

Markeisha Haynes

docs.title: Review of Blue Bottle Coffee
docs.text:
Google review of Blue Bottle Coffee (1 out of 5, by Samir Joshi, 8 months ago): I go to blue bottle when i need coffee early in the mornings, before the local shops open.  To be fair, it's been a great experience for my previous trips but not this time.  They started a promo today for a new drink but HQ didn't include in their email that the promo was only available through their app.

That's not the store's fault and I was fine downloading the app, though i was hoping to just get the discount since that's why I made the trip to the store... but the manager / sr. barista immediately got aggressive, went on a power trip and kept telling me she has the email and I was wrong (she's incorrect, I've read the email multiple times).

What should've been a simple, cordial interaction turned super frustrating with a manager who wanted to make sure she got the last word in.  It's something that just doesn't happen with local owners and this location has lost a customer.

docs.title: Review of The Bungalow Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of The Bungalow Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Karo Karapetyan, 5 months ago): The Bungalow in Santa Monica is always such a fun place to end the night. The atmosphere is lively, relaxed, and full of energy, with a great outdoor vibe that feels very Santa Monica-i. The lighting, music, crowd, and patio setup make it feel like a casual beachside house party.

Whenever I go to Wally’s in Santa Monica with friends, we almost always finish the night at The Bungalow, and it never disappoints. It is the kind of place where everyone seems to be having a good time, whether you are there for drinks, conversation, or just to enjoy the energy of the crowd.

The space has a great mix of indoor and outdoor areas, and the ambiance at night is especially fun. It is perfect for groups, casual drinks, and keeping the night going after dinner. The Bungalow has become one of those reliable Santa Monica spots that always delivers a good time. Highly recommend it for anyone looking for a fun, social, and upbeat place to hang out.

docs.title: Review of The Bungalow Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of The Bungalow Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by eileen flores, 8 months ago): We had the most amazing time at Bungalow Santa Monica for Valentine’s Day! My girls and I got bottle service, and it honestly meant so much to us. This was our first Valentine’s Day being single, and the experience made us feel so special and celebrated.

The vibes were incredible — fun, welcoming, and such a beautiful space. Our server was amazing and so on top of everything. She made us feel completely taken care of and truly at home all night.

Addi at the front was also so kind and welcoming. Her energy set the tone from the moment we arrived, and you can tell the team genuinely cares about their guests.

Also — the cauliflower bites are TO DIE FOR. We ordered three rounds because they were that good haha. Highly recommend trying them.

We felt so blessed to have spent the evening here, and it made the night unforgettable. We will absolutely be coming back!

docs.title: Review of The Bungalow Santa Monica
docs.text: Google review of The Bungalow Santa Monica (4 out of 5, by Ari K, 5 months ago): Great atmosphere. Had a large party for my wife and we were all comfortable and had fun. DJ was grumpy and would not take any requests when people clearly wanted to dance. Parking is an issue. Hotel parking is very expensive so the alternative is street parking.

The drinks were also very good. Fun place to go for a night out!

The best is that they turn into a lot wine bar at night. Get their pizza!!!

Everyone here is nice and haven't experienced anything negative. I always look forward to coming back🥰

docs.title: Review of Bodega Wine Bar
docs.text:
Google review of Bodega Wine Bar (4 out of 5, by J Schane, 3 months ago): Great place to work during the day. Lots of people working here, which creates a productive atmosphere, and it turns into a wine bar at night. The music can get a little loud, and the menu is fairly limited. The bar top tables make for great standing desks.

My biggest complaints are that they don’t serve fresh decaf coffee beans. They use some kind of concentrate instead, and they don’t serve cold brew. Both seem like odd omissions for a coffee shop.

Overall, a great spot with a good vibe that could be even better with a few menu improvements.

docs.title: Review of Bodega Wine Bar
docs.text: Google review of Bodega Wine Bar (4 out of 5, by Marley Stubblefield, 4 months ago): OK, so I went on a date here and it wasn’t too loud but honestly it’s not an intimate setting like I had hoped for a wine bar. I got the hummus platter which tasted pretty good but honestly, it didn’t wow me. I feel like the food and vibes are average. The service is pretty good but it’s not a place that I’m dying to go again kind of just felt like a Normie place. I’ve heard it’s really good for working during the day though so maybe I need to go back and try it again.

docs.title: Review of O'Briens Irish Pub
docs.text:
Google review of O'Briens Irish Pub (1 out of 5, by Amanda, 4 months ago): **ADA DISCRIMINATION**
If you have any ADA handicap, don’t waste your time with this establishment. We tried to enter to watch one of the World Cup games and because my parents approached on scooters, they were immediately denied entrance with the claim that they were not able to seat us, Because they were full. While we stood there asking about any possible area in the back they allowed six or seven more people in behind us. When I asked if we could go in the back patio and did not need a table, my parents could stay in their seats or we could park them out front they said - no they were at capacity. We were disappointed, but understood and began to walk away, but as we begin to walk away one more young lady arrived to go in the man at the door asked her “you’re not a liability are you?” I stood there and watched as she promised not to be a liability. They laughed and he let her in . at that point I turned back around from walking away and told him that this was clearly discrimination. As soon as I said that he’s softened and tried again to tell me if I was there earlier it would’ve made a difference. He tried to tell me it was because I showed up right at game time. Completely unaware of that I heard him ask the patron behind us if she was going to be a liability. It’s one thing to say I’m sorry we’re full. It’s another to at first. Say you have no seats. Still allow more people to enter and then as the person’s with disabilities walk away, you make a liability joke to another patron who you allow to enter. I am a local to this town and already know that it’s not the most friendly bar, but I didn’t know they outright discriminated against persons with disabilities and they think it’s funny. I will be looking at reporting this to the city.

Edit to address response: While I appreciate the apology and recognize the unfortunate and untimely joke you made (I did not read her hat) - You just doubled down on your discrimination in your response. My parents can absolutely stand, you judged without asking. They just can’t walk long distances - because parking is very limited at your establishment, we “walked” from Montana Ave and that’s why they had scooters. I told your other coworker my parents did not need chairs and we could park scooters outside. He was starting to consider the back patio, when he looked back at you and you said we could not enter very definitively. When I told you it felt like discrimination, that would’ve been your opportunity to clarify if we were welcome to stand if possible, but you didn’t. I decided not to argue and call you out for the liability comment because we needed to move on and find somewhere welcoming since the game was starting. (Shout out to Rock-n Pies for great beer, food, multiple big screens, and finding a place to park scooters outside while we joined fans inside).

docs.title: Review of XUNTOS
docs.text:
Google review of XUNTOS (5 out of 5, by Alvaro Hoyos, 6 months ago): Spanish food has a nostalgic place in my heart, so I tend to romanticize every Spanish food meal as I go into them and then get woken up post meal. This was not one of those times.

Xuntos has a pintxos and tapas menu that embodies what I love about Spanish food; the sharing aspect and the ability to experience many more dishes than at other cuisine types (yes, dim sum is up there too). We had 12 or so distinct dishes and the highlights were the croquetas, the anchovies on toast, and the scallops. The lowllights, or meh-lights, were the deviled eggs and the tomato toast; one could have used more flavor (yolk mixture needed more punch) and the other was on the saltier side (and I love salt). Shout-out to the basque whiskey which I don't think I had ever had before and the complimentary rose they gave us with the scallops.

Service was friendly, but seems like they were stretched thin. Either way, it was good and the comp rose was a nice "sorry about the delays". They were accommodating to our patatas bravas with the sauce on the side (french fries for the kids win) and we felt welcomed.

Atmosphere was good, if a bit loud, but I liked the decor, including the scallop shell wall and the various paintings.

Overall, we had a great experience at Xuntos and it is exactly what I imagine when I think of a Spanish meal. Looking forward to the next one.

docs.title: Review of Bar Chloe
docs.text:
Google review of Bar Chloe (1 out of 5, by Madeleine Fahlborn, a year ago): I don’t usually write negative reviews, but I felt compelled to share what happened at this establishment. I came here to celebrate my birthday with a few close friends, including one who had been told that we were not allowed because I brought my dog. She got back to him, named Tommy, that it was a service dog. Instead of receiving a welcoming or respectful response, we were met with hostility and judgment. He questioned what the dog was for and she asked back if he was legally allowed to ask that question. He responded that he was and she responded to ask me directly since it is concerning me personally

The owner took issue with what he called my friend’s “sass”—which in reality was a simple, polite question about accessibility and accommodation for my service animal. Based on that alone, he refused to serve us. On my birthday.

Not only was this shocking and hurtful, it was also discriminatory. Denying service because someone asks about a service dog is not only inhospitable, it’s legally questionable. It felt like we were punished for advocating for basic rights.

We had hoped for a fun, celebratory night. Instead, we left feeling humiliated and disrespected. I would not recommend this place to anyone who expects basic decency—especially if you’re bringing a service animal or have friends who dare to speak up.

Do better.

Google review of Surf Liquor and Wine (4 out of 5, by Itz Hollywoood, a year ago): This visit was a genuinely positive experience, highlighted by the exceptional service from a respectful and helpful staff member. The store's inventory is impressive and convenient, offering more than just liquor—a wide array of snacks, drinks, and even wine are available. Discovering a new shooter  finding a classic Don Julio 1942, on a beautiful California day was an unexpected and delightful surprise.
The prices are quite reasonable for the area, and while there may not be many deals, the straight pricing is fair.
Overall, the atmosphere is vibrant, with cool and unique items, including stylish surf liquor trucker hats. The only potential improvement would be the addition of a restroom, though I understand the limitations given the surrounding establishments.
In general, this place has a great vibe, and I will definitely be returning!

docs.text: Google review of Surf Liquor and Wine (5 out of 5, by Rebecca Klempner, a year ago): I loooove this little shop, conveniently located on Main Street in Santa Monica. They have four or five freezers of ice cream novelties. The prices are normal or close to it, not tourist-trap expensive. There's also an extensive liquor, non-alcoholic beverage, and snack selection. The people at the counter are always lovely. Stroll Main Street with an ice cream or cold drink in hand, stop there on the way to the beach, sit on a bench in front of the library (almost directly across the street), and enjoy an afforable outing without forking over lots of cash. Perfect for a cheap date or a visit with the kids. It's close to a couple of the municipal lots and bus accessible.

docs.title: Review of Haque's Bodega
docs.text:
Google review of Haque's Bodega (1 out of 5, by Rose P, a year ago): This review is long overdue, and I’ve even paused to stop myself from reviewing but today’s experience was unsettling and extremely uncomfortable.

I come here to get my breakfast before work, and on past visits I’ve had very bad customer service. Sometimes it can be because “you’re too early breads not here. Do you see the bread?”  “What do you want I cant hear you, is that all” cold type of interactions. I’ve learned to just deal with it but today was triggering and extremely unprofessional I had to speak out.

As I was getting ready to be checked out and I placed some sugar in my iced coffee and that’s when all went bad. “Next time you tell me to put sugar in. That’s my job. You make a mess.” To which I reply “I can clean it, no problem” this was clearly upsetting to the cashier and it became a bad interaction all together.

Needless to say, his tone and way of communicating with me has not been pleasant and I no longer will be stopping here to get breakfast. As I was leaving I could hear him say “you’re so rude” to which gave me more of a reason to walk away and reflect on how customer service these days has been so sour and unfortunately not seen as an essential part of good business practices.

Lovely area, but this type of treatment is unacceptable

docs.title: Review of CVS
docs.text:
Google review of CVS (5 out of 5, by Pia Glenn, 3 months ago): I live and work in the area and I've been coming to the CVS regularly for about 5 years. The location is a very challenging one in terms of Santa Monica's epidemic of homelessness, however there were some clear staffing and management changes within the past few years that have made this a WONDERFUL location.

There has been clear improvement in every element of the store, and Woody is particularly helpful every time I'm there.

Very special kudos to the amazing Kyle, the Loss Prevention colleague who works at all hours. Kyle is so welcoming and kind, and also quick to make a joke and have customers laughing. He has an especially challenging and crucial role (see above!) and he carries it out with professionalism and warmth. I've also observed him using calmness and empathy to defuse a situation with expertise others in his role lack. Thank you so much to Kyle and the entire team at this location for the way you've stepped up and provided an exceptional experience!

docs.title: Review of CVS
docs.text:
Google review of CVS (1 out of 5, by Spencer Greenberg, 7 months ago): The pharmacy at this location is consistently unreliable and unprofessional. I have been coming here for over five years—primarily because it is close to where I live—but the level of service has deteriorated significantly.

Constant staff turnover, and the new pharmacy manager is by far the most concerning change. She is rude, dismissive, and unnecessarily combative in every interaction.

Instead of helping resolve issues, she has hung up mid-conversation and suggested I be willing to accept only 10% of my prescribed medication and that I “be happy with that”.

A recent prescription was sent to this pharmacy and sat unfilled for two weeks. I repeatedly called and eventually was told, it was ready. Then shortly after I was issued another notification on the app saying it would be 4 weeks, obviously I called again where I was told they can provide only 10 of the 120 tablets prescribed, or “try again next month.”

This is essential medication—not something optional or recreational.

docs.text: Google review of Pharmacy | Kaiser Permanente Santa Monica Medical Office (1 out of 5, by Rachel Moore, 3 years ago): Doctors and nurses are excellent and welcoming. I never have an issue with them. I love my care team. They are excellent at meeting the needs of the patients. However, the pharmacy is a nightmare and that honestly ruins the whole experience. Poor communication and service. No communication on when they close for lunch and no one seems to care. Pharmacy wasn’t open yet when I had my appointment so I said I would come back on my lunch break. Pharmacy was closed with no notice, when they finally did open my stuff wasn’t ready even though the doctor had sent it. Spent half day here for what should have been a 15 minute errand.

docs.title: Review of Pharmacy | Kaiser Permanente Santa Monica Medical Office
docs.text: Google review of Pharmacy | Kaiser Permanente Santa Monica Medical Office (2 out of 5, by Darcy O'Brien-Holt, 2 years ago): Kaiser, are you listening? Your patients really need a pharmacy to be available when we are able to stop by. For most working adults, the lunch break is the most likely time of day to pick up a much-needed prescription. This is common sense, and yet the pharmacy has been closed in/around the lunch slot for YEARS. This is a fixable problem: STAFF NEEDS TO TAKE LUNCH BREAKS IN SHIFTS! HIRE MORE STAFF IF NEEDED TO MAKE THIS HAPPEN. Excuse the all caps, but when I first saw this policy, I figured it was a temporary problem caused by a staffing shortage. Now that it has continued for years, I know it's a choice not to fix the problem. Please, please figure out. Countless hours of your patients' lives are being wasted by this policy.

docs.text: Google review of Ralphs Pharmacy (1 out of 5, by Lisa Uniejewski, 2 years ago): Terrible service. Absolutely deplorable it’s funny! docs.title: Review of Montana Wellness Rx Pharmacy
docs.text:
Google review of Montana Wellness Rx Pharmacy (1 out of 5, by Sabrina Baker, 10 months ago): I had an awful encounter at this pharmacy. The pharmacist, Peter, refused to fill my legitimate prescription and actually questioned its validity. He went so far as to contact my doctor to verify it—as if I was lying. Even after my doctor confirmed everything, Peter still declined to dispense the medication when it came back to him.
What really shocked me was his attempt to split a single prescription into multiple separate fills—clearly a scheme to inflate costs. The level of greed is truly unbelievable. I strongly recommend finding another pharmacy.

docs.title: Review of Montana Wellness Rx Pharmacy
docs.text:
Google review of Montana Wellness Rx Pharmacy (1 out of 5, by Claudia Beck, 10 months ago): Extremely disappointing experience. Peter refused to fill a valid prescription and questioned its legitimacy. He called my doctor, who confirmed the order. The prescription was for ten packs of cream for a burn wound.
At the refill, Peter blocked the order again. He said he would only provide one pack instead of the prescribed ten, which would have increased my cost by ten times. This approach would have raised the pharmacy’s profit and added unnecessary expense for me.
The pattern raised concerns about pricing practices. I do not recommend this pharmacy. His behavior appeared driven by greed.

My review reflects the facts of my experience. The prescription was valid and confirmed by my doctor. Your actions caused delays, wasted time and added stress during an injury recovery. The new pharmacy filled the prescription without questions and supported my well being.

They will deliver too if you are in their area for a nominal fee. Now that we switched, I no longer have to stand in long lines at a national chain and be greeted by rude employees. I  should have switched her prescriptions to Montana Wellness Pharmacy years ago. 5 stars!

Since my dental insurance was set to begin in April, I explained that I would follow up once coverage started so I could understand the insurance benefits and expected out-of-pocket costs.

Over the next several weeks, I made two phone calls and even stopped by the office in person trying to get this information. The only consistent response I received was from a very friendly front desk employee who repeatedly explained how overwhelmed the office was. While I appreciated her professionalism, I never got the answers I needed.

Eventually, I decided to seek treatment elsewhere. To avoid unnecessary radiation and duplicate imaging, I requested that my X-rays be sent to me. The office sent a release form, which I signed immediately online. Three days and a follow-up email later, I still had not received my records, despite having an appointment with my new dentist scheduled for that day.

The dental care itself may be fine, but the administrative side of this practice was extremely frustrating. Poor communication, lack of follow-through, and delays in providing basic patient records made this one of the worst healthcare experiences I've had in recent years.

docs.text:
Google review of Sara Larbi DDS (5 out of 5, by Heidi Fecht, 4 months ago): Our expansion and airway treatment with Dr. Dolgov and his wonderful team has been life changing for both my son and myself!

I found this treatment because my son was experiencing trouble breathing.  He had an underdeveloped jaw and crowded teeth.  We looked into mainstream orthodontics and were told his expansion and breathing might require surgery and an ENT!
I’m so grateful to have found this non invasive approach with The Dentist Lounge, not only offering expansion to his palate, but Myofunctional Therapy to correct his muscular habits and weaknesses, a complete integrative process.

Shortly after beginning to see the affects of the expansion my son experienced, and because I had decades of sleep issues which I learned could be related to airway health, I decided to explore expansion and airway treatment for myself.

My consult and CBCT scan with Dr. Dolgov  proved that I had an underdeveloped jaw (the size of 6 year old’s jaw) and an extremely small airway (the width of a coffee stirrer, and apparently it should be the width of a Boba straw!).  Dr. Dolgov then had me undergo a sleep test, which informed me that I had sleep apnea.  Sometimes my oxygen saturation rate would drop to 80 during the sleep apnea episodes!  My body was waking me up to stay alive.

My whole life of struggling to sleep and feeling sensitive came down to a structural issue!  I had struggled with insomnia since I was a teenager.  I am now 56 years old.  I have always been "sensitive" to stimulation, noises, too many people etc.  I assumed because of my “sensitivity” that I was a light sleeper.  To feel balanced mentally, emotionally and physically I would have to practice a lot of different modalities, exercise, yoga, and meditation in the middle of the night, as well as during the day after being in a situation that my “sensitive nature” would be affected by.

At the 4-month mark of my expansion process I had to keep checking the mirror!  It felt as if my nose had gotten bigger, but it was internally that my nose/airway had expanded… who knew this is how we are meant to breathe!  It has made a world of difference!

I’m halfway through the expansion and airway dentistry treatment now and it is amazing how I feel so balanced with more oxygen getting to my brain and regular deep REM sleep.   Your organs need oxygen!  I am a completely different person.  Dr. Dolgov confirmed it was the lack of oxygen and lack of REM sleep, (which allows your brain to process your day) which led me to be such a sensitive person.  I no longer have to constantly do all these practices to feel balanced and normal in my body.
It has been life changing and medically necessary for my sleep issues, sleep apnea, oxygen saturation and overall wellbeing!

I know two people that have gone the surgery route for the same procedure of palate expansion.  Those people have also had to have orthodontics after getting their surgical expansion.  The Dentist Lounge and Dr. Dolgov’s procedure was not invasive and certainly more cost effective than going the surgery route!  My teeth and mouth never hurt, it has been a gentle and gradual process.  I have been one of Dr. Dolgov’s best patient, wearing my retainers at least 20 hours a day, so I have experienced very rapid results.

We love The Dentist Lounge!  Dr. Dolgov, Dr. Larbi and their entire support staff are wonderful people, a very caring small office of cutting edge professionals.  I urge anyone to explore this life changing health procedure or visit The Dentist Lounge for your regular ongoing dental hygiene care!

I will update with before and after pictures when both my son and I are finished with our treatments!

After a recent car accident shook me up, I finally made a new appointment with Vision Dental —and it felt like I had never left.

What stood out immediately:

1. The same exceptional care

2. The same gentle, attentive dental hygienist

3. The same calm, professional, genuinely kind team

I paid upfront for my services, and the office handled billing my insurance for me so the reimbursement check came directly to me. That alone removed so much stress from the process.

Would I love if they accepted my insurance directly? Of course.
But even without that, I can confidently say: I have not found a better dental team anywhere in Los Angeles.

Why they’re worth it:

1. Two clean, convenient locations

2. Easy parking

3. TVs on the ceiling (a surprisingly big comfort)

4. Beautiful, calming aesthetics

5. Thoughtful, respectful care from start to finish

They somehow make me excited to get my teeth cleaned—which says everything.

If you’re someone who values expertise, gentleness, consistency, and being treated like a human (not a number), Vision Dental is absolutely worth it.

docs.text:
Google review of UCLA Health Spine Center (1 out of 5, by Stephanie Valentin, 4 months ago): This is my first experience with UCLA, and it has been one of the most frustrating healthcare experiences I've had because of this clinic's repeated communication and coordination failures. I can't speak for the doctors, because I only saw one for less than 10 minutes during a quick procedure.

I was initially scheduled incorrectly, which required me to coordinate with my employer's HR department, drive over an hour to the appointment, and pay for parking, only to find out I had been brought in for the wrong appointment. When the appointment was rescheduled, I was given a time window in person by staff, only to receive an email the next day to tell me that the appointment time had apparently changed without any explanation.

Trying to get answers has been nearly impossible. Patients cannot contact the clinic directly and must go through a centralized call center. Throughout the day, I called multiple times seeking clarification regarding my appointment. Each time I was told someone from the office would call me back. No one ever did. Instead, the burden of resolving the clinic's scheduling issues was effectively placed on me.

What makes this especially concerning is that the physician who referred me to this clinic specifically emphasized the importance of carefully confirming scheduling details with the office, which should have been a red flag. Unfortunately, my experience ended up validating that warning.

During a previous procedure with this team, staff appeared confused about which arm was being treated and asked me to confirm the treatment side. Thankfully I caught the issue and corrected it myself. Patients should never feel responsible for catching potential errors during a medical procedure.

Following that same procedure, I was left waiting in a gown for nearly an hour because I had apparently been forgotten and never formally discharged. I eventually had to leave the room and track someone down myself. Also, a side note, the gown they gave me was stained. Just an observation, but definitely gave me pause regarding the cleanliness.

When patients are undergoing procedures, they should not have to repeatedly verify appointment details, chase down staff for information, and act as the final safeguard against preventable mistakes.

I have filed a formal complaint with UCLA which from what I read online is pointless, so this seems to be a systematic issue with the UCLA group, but still hope meaningful changes are made so that future patients, many of whom are already dealing with significant pain and stress, do not have to navigate the same issues.

UPDATE:
I finally received a call from Sabine, who identified herself as the clinic manager. Unfortunately, rather than addressing the concerns I raised, the conversation only reinforced them. If this is the manager, then the whole situation makes complete sense.

At no point was there a recognition of the incorrect scheduling of my appointment or the repeated communication failures I experienced. Instead, I was met with passive aggressiveness and repeatedly gaslit regardless of me conveying what was discussed with their staff in person, and kept referring to the email they sent the day AFTER, which does not match the conversation I had with their staff.

What was most disappointing was the complete lack of accountability, the focus seemed to be on defending the process rather than taking feedback as a way to improve their services.

I sincerely hope UCLA reviews these processes and provides additional training and oversight. And save yourself the stress and avoid this crew, and also take a look at the other reviews, there are some even horrific life altering conditions patients left with at this clinic.

docs.title: Review of UCLA Health Spine Center
docs.text:
Google review of UCLA Health Spine Center (1 out of 5, by Douglas Gordon, a year ago): Dr. Shamie just can’t keep his stories straight. Every time we talk to him, he has a different version of events.

Paralyzed by Surgery:
I went into surgery having full use of my arms, wrists, hands, and fingers. I came out paralyzed in both arms from torso through fingertips. That was over three years ago, but I still have many more years of intensive therapy ahead and may have lost use of my right hand forever.

Surgeon’s Explanation:
None given. Ever.

False Medical Records:
The pre-op and post-op consultation notes, both signed by Dr. Shamie, contain many falsehoods. The pre-op notes say I had much pain, had lost much function, had received extensive therapy, and was told of the risks of my surgery. None of this is true. I had no pain, had lost no function, had received no therapy, and “some pain” was the only risk he ever mentioned. Although his surgery left me paralyzed, the post-op notes make no mention of this, only “some weakness.” He grossly exaggerated my right hand’s grip at 2 of 5 when, in fact, my thumb and fingers were paralyzed.

First Version of Events:
During our first telemedicine call, Dr. Shamie said it is very common for incorrect information to be “automatically” carried over from other patients, effectively telling us that another patient’s inapplicable records were copied and pasted. (UCLA’s Office of Patient Experience confirmed this is not uncommon.) Dr. Shamie told us I could submit a request to correct the records.

Second Version of Events:
I submitted a request to amend the records. Dr. Shamie refused and, after initially telling us how the false records had originated, now said the records were actually true and accurate.

Third Version of Events:
In our second telemedicine call, Dr. Shamie had yet another story. This time, he said the records were written by someone else and, since he had only signed them, he could not correct them. Then he said the strength test he personally performed on me had been done by someone else.

Bottom Line:
Dr. Shamie has
1) left me paralyzed with no explanation,
2) ended my career,
3) caused us extreme and continuing anguish,
4) necessitated many years of intensive, expensive and unreimbursed therapy, and
5) given us three different explanations for his false medical records.

Google review of Tide Cleaners (1 out of 5, by Stephanie Roberts, a month ago): I have loved this business for years. They have genuine old-fashioned customer service, and they do great work! Yet after they were acquired by TIDE I've experienced frustration after frustration with their app. They send me so-called Rewards and Coupons, but then these discounts don't actually SHOW UP on my delivery orders.  For instance, just yesterday I received a nice 25% off coupon for household items (blankets, etc). I was GOING to schedule a pick up (they have a great driver and reliable pickups & deliveries), but guess what? I called the store to verify if the coupon I activated in my app was in their system, and the nice lady said it was not.( Also there is no place to check Household Items on the app, It only offers Dry Cleaning, Laundry and Wash and Fold). THEN she told me the coupon had expired! Yet I just received the notice for it yesterday and it's supposed to be good for a week.
I've absolutely not placed orders before because of all this frustration (aka UX FRICTION).   I would like to suggest to the huge corporation that is TIDE, that it actually hires some nice folks to ANALYZE  their app (for Phone and Desktop) from a consumer's usage and experience perspective.  Imagine the increased revenue you (Tide) might receive if you make it EASY for people to give you their money by making your rewards and coupons actually work.

PS: The  APP DEVELOPERS. may imagine they are regularly sending Tide's loyal customers coupons. But I use their pick-up and delivery service, so are they really sending me COUPONS  when they tell me i have to bring my laundry INTO  the store in order to use the coupon?  hmm?  Sending — that are unusable in one way or another  — does not encourage people to place more orders with them ...  instead it makes them feel they  need a laundry service backup.

Very reliable. Parking lot. Great coffee shops nearby.

- Bring your clothing to May for custom alterations!
- If you need your shoes cleaned, bring them in for a touch-up (i.e. $10 for sneakers and $28 for leather/suede).
- Be very clear up front for a pricing quote and get it in writing for a unique article like shoes or accessories. The gel also wasn't sitting flush at the cuticle so he tried to fixed that too, already looking grown out on day one. It should be a cat eye effect but it’s a plain shimmer.

docs.title: Review of BonLierre Nail Spa
docs.text:
Google review of BonLierre Nail Spa (1 out of 5, by Alexandria G, 5 months ago): Loyal Customer of Years. Complete Service Failure & Ignored Complaints. I called the owner several times as she asked in her reply to my review, she refused to take my calls or call me back. She never made it right.

I have been coming to BonLierre for years and specifically to Brian, whose work I have always valued. Unfortunately my last experience has ended that relationship entirely.

On January 31st I came in for a fill. I was quoted $55 over the phone and charged $65 when I arrived. Brian was overbooked and rushed through my service. On February 2nd -- just two days later -- I emailed the salon detailing the rushed service and the overcharge. I never received a response.
Within weeks, my pinky nail popped off completely. I returned on February 17th to have it replaced and address the lifting. Brian was dismissive, did not speak to me, rushed through the service, and didn't even brush the powder off my nails before finishing. I left with nails in worse condition than when I arrived.
Today, March 6th -- just over a month after my fill -- four nails fell off on their own in a single morning, with a fifth having fallen off over the weekend. The entire product lifted cleanly off my natural nail bed, which is a clear sign of improper prep and bonding failure -- not normal wear.
When I called today I was told "it's been a month, that's normal." It is not normal for an entire set to fall off. Normal wear is growth at the base. What I experienced is a complete product failure due to a rushed, careless service. All other nails, aside from the pinky nail, have lifted from more than half my nail bed, I anticipate they will fall of at some point today as well.

I was a loyal customer who walked to this salon, paid premium prices, and gave every opportunity for this to be resolved quietly. Instead I was overcharged, ignored, and now have to pay out of pocket to fix their mistake. I won't be going back.

Google review of Salty Mane (1 out of 5, by Annie Dempsey, 9 months ago): This was the worst haircut I have ever received.

I booked a same-day haircut with Jordan at 7pm. On the phone, I confirmed I would be paying cash and was told that was fine. When it came time to pay, I was told there was no change available. I offered to Zelle instead, and only then was I told that change was available. I ended up paying $185 in cash for a $150 haircut.

Jordan was kind and personable during the appointment, but the quality of the haircut itself was extremely poor. The cut is uneven, choppy, and poorly blended, with random short pieces throughout and no cohesive shape. I declined thinning shears in the end, but by that point the damage was already done.

I didn’t say anything in the moment because I’m not confrontational and just wanted to leave before getting upset. After getting home and later showing the cut to other professional stylists, I realized how objectively bad the work was.

I initially planned to just pay another professional to fix it and move on. After being encouraged by others, I reached out privately and respectfully to ask for a refund, making it clear I would not post reviews or share photos publicly. That request was refused. The only options offered were to return to the same stylist or see the owner for a revision, neither of which I felt comfortable with given the situation.

I now have to pay additional money elsewhere to correct this haircut.

I appreciate that the salon responded, but refusing a refund while offering only in-house fixes after such a poor result left me feeling unheard. I wish this had been handled differently.
