docs.text:
Google review of Salon Republic Santa Monica on 2nd (3 out of 5, by Marc Christopher, 3 years ago): Title: Mixed Experience at Salon Republic Santa Monica
I had the opportunity to rent a studio at Salon Republic in Santa Monica, and my experience there was a blend of ups and downs. Initially, everything was fantastic. The studio provided a great space for my work, and the ambiance was truly inspiring.

As the COVID situation unfolded, things became more challenging due to constantly changing rules and regulations. However, despite the hurdles, we managed to navigate through the difficulties together, which I appreciated.

However, my overall impression of Salon Republic soured significantly when it was time for me to move out. They presented me with a bill exceeding three thousand dollars, an outrageous amount compared to the mere $150 deposit I had initially paid. They claimed that I had caused damage to the studio that I rented, leaving me baffled and frustrated.

This serves as a word of caution for anyone considering renting from Salon Republic: be aware that they expect the studio to be returned in the exact condition it was when you first moved in no matter how many years you have been there, meaning no account for wear and tear. Failure to meet their standards could result in substantial charges that you may not have anticipated.

In addition, a piece of advice; I'm truly grateful for is stopping the automatic weekly rent deduction from my account well before my departure. Had I not done so, Salon Republic could have easily taken the money from my account without my consent.

Sharing this review is essential because, in situations like these, it's crucial to empower fellow renters with information. While we might not always have advocates in our corner, remember that establishments like Salon Republic have their own support systems.

In the end, my time at Salon Republic had its moments, but the post-rental experience left me disappointed and cautious about similar arrangements in the future.

Check out these insane "before and after" photos of Sara's transitioning my highlighted hair to full-on platinum blonde. I love my hair more than ever and Sara is the reason why. Check her out at Salon Republic!

Here are some tips Sara shared to keep platinum hair bright:
- Use Davines "MINU" and "NUNU" shampoo and conditioner
- Wash only 2-3 times a day
- If you do hot yoga (like me!) just blow it out after class and wear in a loose bun or ponytail
- Keep heating tools to a minimum

docs.title: Review of Equinox Santa Monica
docs.text: Google review of Equinox Santa Monica (1 out of 5, by Medusa Magic, a month ago): Not very clean and not well maintained. For the amount of money I payed for this gym, I expected so much better. The gym is literally always crowded. Classes are crowded, there is always a wait for every machine, machines are frequently broken. There are waiting lists for the pool. I don’t understand how Equinox gets labeled as a premium gym. It’s just expensive for no reason.

docs.title: Review of Equinox Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of Equinox Santa Monica (2 out of 5, by Neda Zarrabi, 6 months ago): I’m really disappointed with my experience here, especially considering how much I’m paying.

For a large part of February, several amenities were unavailable. The steam room was out of order, and the pool was closed for about two weeks. On top of that, even when the pool is open, access is extremely inconvenient. You have to join a waiting list and sometimes wait hours. For example, if you go in the morning hoping to work out, you might not get a pool time until 3 or 4 PM, which defeats the purpose.
Also showers was full of hair .

The text notification system they use for scheduling is also unreliable and frustrating.

Another issue is the lack of classes. There are no dance or Zumba classes for women. A few friends and I brought this up to management, hoping for improvement, but the response we received was very rude. The manager essentially told us, “This is how it is—if you don’t like it, you can leave,” which is unacceptable customer service.

Overall, for the price, the service, availability, and attitude do not meet expectations.

docs.title: Review of Equinox Santa Monica
docs.text: Google review of Equinox Santa Monica (3 out of 5, by mahya sabet, 5 months ago): The atmosphere is good, but the machines are very old. Most of the towels are extremely old, and the shower area doesn’t feel very clean because everything is outdated. The only thing I really liked was that some doors on the 3rd floor open toward the ocean, with a great ocean view, fresh air, and a very nice atmosphere. I just wish the place had some remodeling.

docs.title: Review of Equinox Santa Monica
docs.text: Google review of Equinox Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by DR, 8 months ago): This gym has gotten way better since the new Santa Monica location opened down the road. It's far less crowded now, especially during January rush. It's also one of the more interesting locations I've been to as far as layout across Boston, NYC and SoCal.

docs.title: Review of Equinox Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of Equinox Santa Monica (1 out of 5, by Igor Sokolov, 7 months ago): Scam when it comes to cancelling membership. First they say they have no authority to cancel it at the front desk, then they send you a cancellation link. You answer all the annoying questions and then when you press cancel it says an error has occurred. Then you go back to the front desk and they are so used to this question (obviously happens every time) they give you a card of the manager who btw doesn’t have a phone number, so you have to write them an email and I’m sure they will try their aggressive marketing technique to keep you on file. Really? And that’s the premium gym? Thanks. Never again.

Upd. Was able to cancel through the link after a few attempts, but I’m keeping this review in case someone has the same issue.

docs.title: Review of JOHN REED Fitness
docs.text:
Google review of JOHN REED Fitness (1 out of 5, by Lewis Sessoms, 4 months ago): On Saturday around 1:38pm, My partner and I, attempted to visit the smoothie bar. The female employee with the blue hair was conversing with staff member (mostly), and advised that she was the only one working and could not make a smoothie at that time.

I asked if the other lady was an employee, and she advised that she was a trainer.

Now my home location is DTLA, and I know for fact that the front desk person (even when there is only one person on duty) will go over to the smoothie stand to take the order of a paying customer. I, for the life of me, cannot understand why this employee could not perform that same action. Especially given that checkin for this location is fully automated, so the need for her at that post was very low. 5-10 minutes to make two smoothies (money) should not have interrupted her minuscule duties.

This is the exact reason that this location has the worst reviews; it’s due to staffing attitude and behavior. Your employees really believe that are above the program. They do not properly greet guest when arriving or departing your gym. Instead they find more importance in their conversation with employees, than actually doing their job beyond folding towels. Needless to remind, my membership dues contribute to their pay, which means Im paying for subpar service.

I implore you to better train your employees in critical thinking, customer service, and business savvy. As a business owner myself, an entire day or even one or two minutes of missing sales simply because you would rather engage in conversation than making smoothies, would result in the immediate termination of that employee.

Also, when I called to ask for the manager’s direct email address, I was simply told no. Another issue I’ve never had at DTLA.

docs.title: Review of JOHN REED Fitness
docs.text:
Google review of JOHN REED Fitness (5 out of 5, by Patrick Martin, a year ago): IMO top gym in Santa Monica - newer weights/equipment than Equinox and a fraction of the cost! Solid array of free weights, machines, and cardio equipment + a CrossFit training space and turf for sled work and an outdoor area to take in some of that SoCal Vitamin D! Staff up front are always helpful and friendly, and the gym is as clean as a whistle. Smoothy bar and DJ are the cherry on top! And of course, like everywhere in Santa Monica, full of fit, beautiful people!

Can’t comment on the classes because they’re not my thing but seems like they have a large variety with lots going on everyday.

Only gripes: no sauna, could use more intense cardio equipment like a Jacob’s Ladder or curved self powered treadmill (assault style), as well as some of the influencer types seem to leave their weights and mats on the ground and then bounce - come on people!

docs.text:
Google review of Barry's Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Nzinga Goodwin, 7 months ago): This has to be my new all time favorite Barry’s!

I accidentally showed up here on the wrong day/ time & the Barry’s crew managed to turn what could have been a stressful, frustrating situation into a beautiful morning! I was greeted with such kindness by the mgr Pepper, who took the time to help me find my friend, and toured me around the stunning, sparkling clean facility!

I met the amazing crew, and Zahra assisted me in signing up for my next class, walked me through the process, and provided helpful training tips. I left excited for my next class, and so incredibly thankful for the team here that goes the extra mile for clients!

docs.title: Review of Sweat Yoga
docs.text:
Google review of Sweat Yoga (4 out of 5, by Yamit Florentin, 3 years ago): Come EARLY, even 15-20 minutes before class, not only to be able to find parking but also to check in (there is a screen by the front desk) and, most importantly- to find and secure a spot for your mat!
All the other reviews pointing out how packed the class is are correct.
Sweat Yoga needs to change that. Especially in a hot room, you want enough space to move your body freely. They maximize profit by squeezing as many people as possible into a hot, sweaty, medium-sized room. I've tried CorePower Yoga (both locations, on 2nd Street and Wilshire), and their classes are much less crowded.

The instructor, Isabel Galler, was excellent; she knew what she was doing and how to keep us motivated and focused. She guided us with her voice soft but firm voice. Are you in good shape? Hot Yoga will humble you really quickly! I had to leave the room for a minute about three times to catch a breath and cool my body a bit.
At the end of the flow, you get a cold, wet, small towel to help your body cool down and recover. I definitely felt rejuvenated after the session.

The women's bathrooms and showers can get crowded. There are lockers in the women's restroom with a lock and code.
The customer service at the front desk could be better. As I walked in, I wasn't greeted in any way.
Street metered parking: If you come to the 6:30 AM class, you will find parking quickly and can put money in the meter at 8 AM so that parking will be free.

docs.title: Review of IRON Fitness Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of IRON Fitness Santa Monica (1 out of 5, by Emma Nguyen, 8 months ago): I had a really frustrating experience here and won’t be coming back.

I completely understand that their free pass is only for first-time visitors. My issue is that their own team told me I was eligible. Someone from the gym personally called me to schedule a free session, and I even double-checked over the phone before driving out. They confirmed they had my info on file and said I was good to come in for my free day.

So I made the drive, showed up, and then was told the pass wasn’t valid (because although I had never used the pass before, I had gone once via ClassPass and that apparently excluded me from using the one free day pass…) and I’d be charged. At that point, I wasn’t going to just turn around after wasting my time and gas. It’s ridiculous that their team couldn’t acknowledge the miscommunication or take responsibility for approving me in the first place. I’ll be disputing the charge.

On top of that, parking was very limited, the bathrooms were dirty, sauna situation is a joke, and the equipment situation was not great. Very limited machines and a line just to use the treadmill.

Overall, worst customer service and not worth the hassle.

docs.title: Review of CorePower Yoga - Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of CorePower Yoga - Santa Monica (2 out of 5, by Nonye Nugent, 6 months ago): I tried the one-week free trial while on vacation and wanted to share some feedback.

What I enjoyed:

- The music brought great energy to the classes; it was noticeably louder than my home studio, which made the experience more engaging.
- The staff were consistently welcoming and greeted me with smiles each time I attended.
- The $4 mat rental felt reasonable and convenient.
- Overall, the classes provided a solid and effective workout.

Opportunities for improvement:

- With the higher music volume, adjusting instructor microphone levels would make a big difference. At times, it was difficult to clearly understand cues and instructions.
- Cleanliness could be improved. The rental mats had an unpleasant odor, the cleaning wipes for equipment were dried out, and the mirrors appeared unclean during multiple visits (Wednesday and Friday), suggesting they hadn’t been maintained regularly. See photo.
- A brief introduction to the CorePower methodology for new participants would be helpful. Since students are encouraged to arrive 15 minutes early, that time could be used to provide a quick overview. As a first-time visitor, I occasionally felt unsure about certain aspects of the class, even though I was able to keep up.

Overall, I am not sure I have interest in returning to corepower, but glad I tried it!

docs.title: Review of CorePower Yoga - Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of CorePower Yoga - Santa Monica (4 out of 5, by Yamit Florentin, 3 years ago): My very first time I am doing Hot Yoga. I've tried many fitness studios; CrossFit, pilates, Yoga, Barry's Bootcamp, circuit training, beach workout, etc. Hot Yoga is a lot more challenging than any other workout I've done. The heat in the room makes your body sweat right away, and you burn so many calories.
ProTip: Set up your mat near the door; it makes the heat a little more bearable.

The studio is clean and aesthetic, but I wish their customer service improved. They run a Facebook ad advertising a free trial.
From just looking at the ad, it needed to be clarified if the free week starts on the same day you signed up or later when you start coming.
When I arrived at the studio the first time, they said my free week is expired, but I explained Ive never been there before and that this was my first time. I had to wait until after the session to speak to the manager to sort it out.

They DO NOT provide a mat or towel. You can bring your own or rent it from them; it's $2 to rent a towel and $8 to rent a Yoga mat.
The women's bathroom has showers, but they do not offer bath towels. Bring your own if you plan to get ready to work after the workout.

If you are looking for a fitness studio where you can also build a community, it isn't the right place. People don't talk to each other here, they keep to themselves, and some are snobby; it's LA, so I shouldn't be surprised. People here come to work out and leave; they are not here to root for you in any way. I understand that some people prefer it that way, and that's ok; to each his own.

My favorite instructors were Janelle and Skylar. They lead a great flow!

Google review of CorePower Yoga - Santa Monica (1 out of 5, by Zaso, 8 months ago): I’m writing this on behalf of my sister after she’s told me of  what has happened at CorePower Santa Monica …. It’s completely unacceptable.

She woke up and drove all the way to Santa Monica for a 7:30 AM Sculpt class. About 30 minutes into class, the entire room started smelling like straight gasoline. Not a faint odor;  a strong, alarming fume smell. The class had to stop and everyone left the room in a panic. No one should ever have to worry about inhaling gas fumes in the middle of a heated workout.

What makes this worse is that this isn’t an isolated issue at this studio:
• A 6:00 AM class was canceled 10 minutes before start time — after she was already THERE at the studio

This studio feels completely unreliable and poorly managed. People structure their schedules around these classes and pay premium prices expecting professionalism and safety. Between last-minute cancellations, no-show instructors, and now a potential safety hazard, it’s beyond frustrating.

CorePower Santa Monica needs to seriously get its act together. This level of inconsistency and disregard for members’ time and safety is unacceptable.

docs.title: Review of Fred Fitness
docs.text:
Google review of Fred Fitness (5 out of 5, by David Choi (djc200), 9 months ago): This review is long overdue—maybe because Fred still feels like one of LA’s best hidden gems (for now). I’ve been training here since June, and I can confidently say it’s helped me tremendously as a biohacker, bodybuilder, L2 CrossFit coach (~10 years as an athlete/trainer), and now as an avid runner.

I’ve been biohacking for a decade, produced my own live biohacking show (@biohacktheworld), and I'm constantly seeking the next frontier of fitness. I experiment with all kinds of supplements and training modalities, but I still prefer the all-natural, no-nonsense side of fitness and biohacking—and Fred fits that perfectly.

Here are some of my favorite selling points for Fred Fitness:
You never have to change weights or guess what to lift. Seriously—this is a game changer. It makes every session more efficient, especially if you like to superset. You get lean and strong in a fraction of the time. For anyone with a busy schedule or a day job, this one feature alone makes your fitness goals so much more achievable. (Pro tip: you can have the trainers help you adjust the starting and ending position on each of the machines so you're training from the most stretched position for optimal muscle hypertrophy)

The circuit training area keeps everyone moving. No standing around waiting for machines. If you're time-crunched, this setup is perfect—you stay in flow and your workout never drags. (Pro tip: I split the upper and lower body circuits and will do 2-4 rounds of upper one day and 2-4 rounds of lower another day)

Built-in negative/eccentric training. This was the main selling point for me. The machines automatically increase resistance on the eccentric phase—something you just can’t replicate consistently with traditional free weights. Eccentrics are essential for muscle hypertrophy, period. (Pro tip: do 2-3 sets of Negative and a final set in Adaptive mode to go to complete failure)

The InBody scans + AI BioAge system are legit. It even simulates your VO₂ max. I compared mine to a real VO₂ test, and the numbers were close enough that I trust the trends. I’m 47, and with all the strength training, rowing, and running I do (I train almost daily), I’ve worked my BioAge down to 26. I feel better now than I actually did at 26!

Runner-friendly strength machines. They have everything a runner needs: leg press, leg extension/curl, single-leg kickback, hip thrust, back extension, adductor/abductor. No calf machine, but dumbbells get the job done. For runners, this lineup is elite.

One of the best cable machines around. Tons of accessory work options. If you're like me and love dialing in the small details, you’ll use this nonstop.

Mat Pilates 5x a week. My wife loves this. We’re signing up for the 12-month commitment when we return from Asia in March—it brings the membership down to just $100/month, which is honestly wild for everything you get.

They partner with Siphox for bloodwork. Think Function Health or Superpower, but more convenient because it’s at-home finger-prick testing. As a biohacker, this is a huge plus.

The crowd is a great mix. You’ll see beginners, everyday fitness enthusiasts, and people who really follow the science of muscle-building. Anyone who appreciates smart programming and technology-driven training will love what the eGym machines and cardio equipment can do. Never has fitness been more accessible and achievable for all!

There's a great recovery area with leg compression, red light masks, and more.

I'll update this review as time goes on but all said, this place is ace!

docs.title: Review of Anytime Fitness
docs.text:
Google review of Anytime Fitness (4 out of 5, by Angela Vasquez, 6 months ago): I started at Anytime Fitness through One Pass Select with my work insurance, but this location opened in Summer 2025 and is way closer to my job, so my membership transferred here. I ended up getting a membership since this location doesn’t accept insurance-based memberships, which was disappointing, but hitting the gym right after work is honestly the only reason I stay consistent. I’ve been coming to this location since then, mostly after work, which is their busiest time. I still go to other gyms through One Pass, but this is the one I come to the most because of how convenient it is. I already know if I go home first… I’m not leaving again 😅

It does get busy during peak hours, but that’s expected anywhere at that time. However, my only real gripe is people supersetting during peak hours and holding multiple machines. That said, even when it’s busy, it’s still less crowded than other gyms I’ve tried at peak times. I do appreciate that some machines are dual-use for space saving (like the multi press, leg curl/extension, and adduction/abduction).

Equipment-wise, I feel like it would be perfect if they added an angled hack squat machine. Bonus points for a lateral raise machine, dual 45 hip extension, seated dip, abdominal crunch machine, and a seated bicep curl machine...not the preacher, but the one with the arm pads on the sides (not that all of these could realistically fit, but still).

I’ll be honest, I don’t even know exactly how much I’m paying. It’s definitely on the pricier side, and I’m pretty sure there was a promotion when I signed up that ended. But I’m basically paying for convenience, and it’s still comparatively less packed than other gyms at their busiest. I kind of rotate between gyms depending on what machines I need and like, but I definitely prefer coming here for glute/hamstring days, cardio, and back days. I do shoulders/abs/arms somewhere else.

Overall, still one of my go to gyms because of the convenience, cleanliness, and vibes, but please add an angled hack squat :)

docs.title: Review of Power Yoga East
docs.text:
Google review of Power Yoga East (5 out of 5, by YogaFieldNotes, 9 months ago): Summary:  If you’re looking for a high-energy flow, this isn’t that.  But if you want a thoughtful, breath-centered practice that helps you slow down, feel your body, and cultivate steadiness, this class is your go-to.

The Space:  This studio is a second-floor loft with tall windows and skylights overhead, so natural light pours in.  The room is spacious, uncluttered, and simply arranged, which amplifies the quiet, reflective tone of the class.

The Class:  We began with a collective Om and alternate-nostril breathing, then moved into a steady sequence of Sanskrit-cued postures rather than a flowing practice.  (I did have to peek at others for a few poses!)

Because there was no music, every breath, footstep, and verbal cue became part of the atmosphere.  At first, I felt more self-aware, but that actually drew me deeper into my breath.  I ended up finding it rather powerful and reflective.

The Teacher:  Jerome was warm and attentive, especially with first-timers.  He introduced himself, encouraged me to place my mat wherever I felt comfortable, and offered hands-on adjustments that invited the body to relax deeper rather than push harder.

Vibe:  His use of Sanskrit cueing, paired with steady breathwork (beginning with a collective Om and alternate-nostril breathing), created a classical, contemplative tone.  This was not a flow; it was a deliberate exploration of posture and breath.

Community:  The overall atmosphere felt community-oriented.  People were chatting with one another as they gathered up their belongings after class, which made the space feel friendly and welcoming.

Practical Notes:  I also loved that this is a drop-in studio.  There’s no advance sign-up needed, just show up with your mat.  Parking is free right outside.  It's a DONATION-BASED class.  Welcome to all!

Quick Note:  The class isn’t heated, but with so much sunlight streaming in, a gentle natural warmth builds throughout the practice.

docs.text:
Google review of Sweat 60 Personal Training - Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Nancy B, 3 months ago): Coach Jordan Kerner is a life-changer. I began working with her one-on-one at Sweat 60 about 5 months ago and have benefitted tremendously in my strength, fitness, and mobility. The workouts she designs are always changing, and I’m amazed each time how she manages to tailor them perfectly to my pace and goals. docs.title: Review of Sweat 60 Personal Training - Santa Monica
docs.text:
Google review of Sweat 60 Personal Training - Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Leslie Ventura, 5 months ago): I spent quite a bit of time trying out different classes after moving to the area, and Sweat60 quickly became my favorite. I’m happy to say I’ve since become a regular. From the trainers to the members, everyone has been incredibly warm and welcoming. The classes offer a great mix of strength training and cardio, and it’s a bonus that you get to enjoy being outdoors.

I’ve especially loved getting to know the trainers—they bring such positive energy and make it easy to keep coming back and genuinely enjoy working out. A special shoutout to Sean, Cruz, and Sam for constantly challenging me and pushing me to improve. Huge thanks as well to Jordan and Jada for their encouragement during those tough early mornings—it really makes a difference. And to Jamaal, thank you for always being so helpful and welcoming (now we just need you to start teaching some morning classes!).

Sweat60 has truly become something I look forward to every week—thank you for creating such an incredible community.

docs.title: Review of Sweat 60 Personal Training - Santa Monica

When I started training at Sweat 60, every employee greeted me by name and went out of their way to say hello which was incredibly welcoming and continues to happen each week. My progress in strength, balance, and form has improved drastically and his training sessions are motivating, carefully planned and measured to increase overall strength while targeting specific areas. Sweat 60 is an incredible gym that is well managed, super clean, uber friendly, and has highly skilled, professional trainers. A shout out to Grant for his excellent work and can't recommend him enough!!

docs.title: Review of Allegiate Gym
docs.text:
Google review of Allegiate Gym (5 out of 5, by Raffi Terteryan, 6 months ago): I’ve always been an active person focused on playing various sports, but hated weight lifting / commercial gyms. I found them boring and I wouldn’t push myself to exert a lot of effort or go consistently. As I got busier in my career and lost the time to play the sports I normally played, my physical health took a toll.

I’ve been coming to Allegiate for about 3 times a week 5 months now. The staff is knowledgeable and friendly. The programming is well crafted and pushes you. I’ve gained a great amount of strength in a relatively short amount of time and the focus on mobility in addition to strength has greatly improved my weaker lower back.

Overall, can’t say enough good things about the place.

docs.title: Review of Allegiate Gym
docs.text:
Google review of Allegiate Gym (5 out of 5, by jordan yrastorza, 7 months ago): I have been an athlete my entire life, ex college baseball player. I came off a really bad knee injury in 2023 from Brazilian Jiu Jitsu and after being cleared I couldn’t find a way back to getting in shape with out my knee being a road blocker.
I researched local gyms and Allegiate stood out to me because the stood for injury prevention and recovery. So I did a trail class. I walked in and I was greeted as if the coaching staff already knew who I was and asked about my injury. The vibe gave instant flash backs to my college baseball weight lift days. As I struggled with doing anything associated with legs the coaches not only found accommodating methods for me to
Get as much of the lift in, but they were supportive when I would hit my stopping point and come
Up with stretches or alternative exercises so I can still get my lift in!
After 3 months of consistently going, the night and day difference with walking alone was amazing! I have been here at Allegiate for over 140 classes and I’m now able to run and put weight on my knee!
I sadly am moving away and have to leave Allegiate but the coaching staff genuinely care about your well being and getting you into or back into the best shape of your life. All you gotta do is show up and do the work!

Thank you Allegiate Coaching Team!

docs.title: Review of Allegiate Gym
docs.text:
Google review of Allegiate Gym (5 out of 5, by Alyssa Farraye, 8 months ago): I’ve been training at Allegiate for the past 2.5 years, and it has truly been one of the best investments I’ve ever made in my health, and I don't say that lightly.

Before Allegiate, my strength training experience was basically nonexistent. I mostly relied on Pilates and long walks. I always wanted to build muscle and get stronger, but I had no idea where to start. Programming workouts, figuring out exercises, sets, reps..it all felt overwhelming and intimidating.

A friend who works in athletics at UCLA recommended Allegiate, so I decided to give it a try. I started with personal training for the first 6 months..then moved into Strength Class, and after about a year of Strength Class, I moved into the advanced Team Class.

The progress I’ve made since then has honestly been life-changing. When I started, I couldn’t do a single pull-up. Now I can do four. I struggled to do 1-2 push-ups, now I can do 10+. I couldn’t deadlift even half my bodyweight, and now I’m lifting 1.7x my bodyweight. Seeing those kinds of gains over time has completely changed how confident and capable I feel.

What sets Allegiate apart, especially in LA, is that it’s not flashy or focused on aesthetics or “influencer” culture. It’s about the fundamentals: smart programming, proper form, and getting stronger in a sustainable way. You don’t have to figure anything out on your own. You just show up, follow the program, and get coached.

The coaching is incredible. Every coach knows you by name, explains the “why” behind what you’re doing, and makes strength training approachable instead of intimidating. I’ve learned so much, and I’ve built real relationships here, people I call my friends. The community is just as special. Classes feel like training with the same group of people each week..it’s supportive, consistent, and feels more like a team than a typical gym.

Allegiate taught me that fitness doesn’t have to be complicated..stick to the basics, stay consistent, and results come. I’m stronger than I’ve ever been, and I can’t recommend this place enough.

docs.title: Review of Allegiate Gym
docs.text:
Google review of Allegiate Gym (5 out of 5, by Craig Henderlite, 10 months ago): I’ve been at Allegiate for 2.5 years now. Allegiate is hands down the best gym if you want to get stronger and see results, no matter your experience level. My review is overdue…

- Started with an ankle / foot injury that I was told would never get back to 100%. After working through the strength and now team program, the pain and instability is gone.

- Down 4 (yes, four) waist sizes so far with a (somewhat) healthy diet. Easily in the best shape since starting my career 10+ years ago. Feel awesome and can’t wait to see more results over the next year.

- Coaches and members are great people. Extremely supportive environment, and not intimidating despite lifts being challenging. Have made several close friends from class and love going in. Coaches are all over everyone in a good way and watch your form.

Just a few points. Stick to the program and you’ll see results!! Sign up!!!

docs.text: Google review of Oak Park - The Home of CrossFit Los Angeles (5 out of 5, by Krysta Rose, a year ago): I dropped I to Oak Park on my vacation to complete the Open 25.3 workout, looking for a CrossFit gym in the area, and my experience was fantastic, beyond my expectations! This gym has the most welcoming coaches and community with a top notch facility. The indoor outdoor concept was super nice with the sun and palm trees. Jamie, the manager, was incredibly kind for allowing me a space to complete the Open. I would highly recommend this CrossFit gym to anyone visiting the area if you want a space to meet new and incredible people. Thank you Oak Park for the fantastic workout!

docs.title: Review of Oak Park - The Home of CrossFit Los Angeles
docs.text:
Google review of Oak Park - The Home of CrossFit Los Angeles (5 out of 5, by Brandy Jones-Breth, 2 years ago): I can't say enough positive things about my experience at Oak Park. My husband and I are both members and it’s a time for us to bond and become better and stronger parents for our two kids. As a busy mom, finding time for self-care can be challenging, but this gym has truly been a game-changer for my mental and physical well-being.

First and foremost, the coaches are simply outstanding. They are dedicated to helping each member reach their fitness goals no matter the fitness levels.  Oak Park provides a family-friendly and inclusive environment. It’s a positive and motivating atmosphere and the coaches makes every workout enjoyable and effective.

One coach, in particular, Char, has made a significant impact on my postpartum journey. As a mom herself she personally understands my needs and tailors my private training sessions. Her expertise, encouragement, and unwavering support have been instrumental in my fitness transformation. She also coaches the Women’s Class which has been a game changer for my confidence. It’s like a bonus that I have a female and mom community that is empowering and supportive for the unique needs of women.

docs.title: Review of Oak Park - The Home of CrossFit Los Angeles
docs.text: Google review of Oak Park - The Home of CrossFit Los Angeles (5 out of 5, by Erik Moreno, 2 years ago): I have been a member of Oak Park (and its predecessor CrossFit LA) since 2012.  I have absolutely loved my time there - I keep coming back for the incredible workouts and coaching...but I stay because of the community.  This community is like my second home and second family.  The coaches truly care about my overall well being (physically and emotionally), I get world class instruction (I have learned to row, Olympic weight lifting, gymnastics among a myriad of other skills) in an environment that is safe and fun.  The focus on functional health (including stretching and injury prevention) will help me stay fit and healthy for years to come.  So grateful to be part of this incredible gym and its awesome community of like-minded individuals.

docs.title: Review of Oak Park - The Home of CrossFit Los Angeles
docs.text: Google review of Oak Park - The Home of CrossFit Los Angeles (5 out of 5, by Elana Schuldt, 2 years ago): I can’t say enough great things about Oak Park, the trainers and the community. I work out 1-1 with Char and also attend her weekly women’s class. The coaching, workouts and care Char provides are top notch. In a few months I’ve built muscle mass, toned up and had a lot of fun. The women I’ve met through class are so special - dynamic, fun, interesting. The facilities are great, they have everything you could possibly need. Oak Park is an amazing community to be a part of!

docs.text:
Google review of Piper Preschool - Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by J C, in the last week): We absolutely love Piper. From the moment we walked through the doors on my tour, we could feel how much thought, care and love had gone into creating such a special place. My husband was kind of checked out on all of our preschool tours until this one. He was locked in on Piper.

It feels welcoming, sweet, and thoughtful in ways where it feel less like a traditional school and more like a second home. We were worried about all the craziness with schools in this area, but Piper put all of that to rest. From the materials, to the classrooms, to the playground, to all the little learning centers, every detail feels intentional.

The teachers are truly what make Piper so special. Not only are they amazing, kind, patient and nurturing, but they act like they love their job and that makes all the difference. Our kids absolutely love going to school, and as parents, there's no better feeling than seeing your children excited to walk through the doors each morning. Knowing they're surrounded by people who care about them, encourage their curiosity and celebrate their individual personalities gives us so much peace of mind. I really can't say enough good things about Piper. It just feels really right in there.

One of our kids' favorite things about Piper is the creek. It's such a unique and magical feature that we didn't find at any other preschools. Watching the kids explore, play, get their hands dirty and discover the world around them is exactly what childhood should look like. Between the creek, gardens and art spaces, this school creates an outdoor environment where learning feels natural. The kids get to be kids while gaining confidence, independence, creativity and a love of learning.

We're going on our second year and we couldn't be happier. It's the kind of place that makes you appreciate how important these early years are and how much of a difference the right environment and the right people can make. Our kids are happy, excited to learn and surrounded by teachers who make them feel loved and supported. Piper has created something truly special, and we're so grateful to be part of it.

Also, they have a whole floor for parents to work. I haven't done it yet, but it's beautiful. We love Piper.

docs.title: Review of Palisades Preschool
docs.text:
Google review of Palisades Preschool (5 out of 5, by L.A.S., 6 months ago): We feel so grateful to be part of the Palisades Preschool community. Our daughter started in the toddler program at 18 months and is now in the youngest preschool classroom. The experience has been exceptional every step of the way.

The toddler program alone is worth mentioning—many parents call it “magical,” and that’s exactly how it feels. Each week, the teachers and atelieristas create a warm, beautiful environment with soft lighting and thoughtfully designed exploration areas. The children attend with their parents or caregivers, play together, and share a snack where they sit at tables and serve themselves. It’s a gentle, joyful introduction to school. We loved that the teacher from the youngest preschool classroom leads the program, which makes the transition to drop-off the next year feel more familiar.

As our daughter moved into the preschool this year, we were struck by the level of intention and care. The teachers are dedicated and knowledgeable. They meet every afternoon to reflect on the day and thoughtfully plan for what the children need next. They collaborate with atelieristas each week to bring in creative, meaningful materials—clay, natural elements, artist-grade paints, wire, light and shadow, and storytelling—so the children can learn to explore and express themselves through different media.

The campus itself is also special—lush outdoor spaces with gardens, trees, and imaginative elements created by the children, making it feel like a little world of its own. It's fun to see the children watering the plants, playing in the river rock bed with the water pump, and watching the butterfly cocoons that form.

We’ve also seen a meaningful transformation in our daughter. She used to be cautious and slow to warm in new situations, but during her time here, she has blossomed. Her confidence in exploring materials and engaging with her peers has grown significantly. She now dives into art (happily getting messy!) and interacts with her friends with ease, joy, and connection.

One of the most striking moments for us was hosting our daughter’s class for her birthday. Watching the children interact outside of school, we were amazed by how calm, kind, and collaborative they were. They invited each other to play, took turns easily, shared materials, and navigated social situations with awareness and respect. The parents were able to step back and hang out, which felt so different from other gatherings outside of the preschool that we’ve attended. It was clear that the children’s social-emotional skills are being thoughtfully cultivated at school every day.

And, while we are still far from the kindergarten process, we’ve connected with families of Palisades alumni whose children have gone on to some of the most well-regarded schools in Los Angeles, including Brentwood School, The Village School, and Crossroads, along with many other fantastic private and public schools. It’s reassuring to see how strong the foundation is for the years to come.

That's not surprising given that it feels like everything the school does is grounded in what’s best for the child. Even the decision to offer only morning programs reflects a deep respect for young children’s need for rest and the teachers’ need for thoughtful preparation.

Palisades Preschool is a special place, and we feel incredibly lucky that our daughter and our family are part of this community.

docs.title: Review of Palisades Preschool
docs.text:
Google review of Palisades Preschool (5 out of 5, by HPM J, a year ago): I truly cannot imagine a more loving, thoughtful educational environment than this for my two young children (nearly 3 and nearly 5). We were at another preschool for a year before PPS. It was chaotic to say the least and has since shut down due to low enrolment. I was extremely nervous - feeling at risk of making another poor choice, but I was instantly put at ease by the warmth of the teachers and the community as a whole.

The head of the school is a wondrous person for fostering such a beautiful spirit of social and emotional development here. They have a dedicated art teacher who helps the children to create the MOST expressive and thoughtful pieces of work. A music teacher who attends weekly who is unrivalled. A kitchen where the kids make and taste brand new foods regularly. Not to mention extremely high teacher ratios (we are currently in a class with 3 teachers for 12 kids) and huge amounts of time outside on a beautiful yard. And wow are those teachers magic. I don't know how I will bear leaving them when we eventually have to go.

I'm sad to see another review complain about their children being behind in Kindergarten. The Kindergartens I have toured for next year have all expressed that they support children at all stages of reading/writing, including zero - it is their first year of official school after all. All the educational philosophies I care about support play-based education from 2-5. For me it's not a race. I feel lucky to have found a beautiful preschool in which my kids are thriving.

EDIT: A year later, our older child is now in Kindergarten. It's a prestigious elementary school and his teachers have described him as having been extremely well prepared for Kindergarten. Thanks PPS!

docs.text: Google review of Maple Tree Academy (5 out of 5, by LD, 10 months ago): We love MTA! My baby has been going there since he was 7 months. As first time parents, we were so nervous. But MTA is great. Before you start, the administrator personally come to your house for a meet and greet, and goes over everything, explaining what to bring etc. All the teachers are super sweet, I don't know how they remember each kids' parents, even when the non-primary parent picks them up, but they do. They ask you every morning if there's any specific instructions for the day. My baby had eczema and they were good about applying the lotion we gave them. Because they also speak Spanish to the kids, he was saying 'agua' before he could say 'water'. I like that they don't only do play, but they have a curriculum and teach the kids too. They're really good with communicating through the app. One day, he saw another kid eating apples and he said he wanted some, so the teacher msged us "he wants apples". My baby really loved all his teachers. Whenever there are situations such as when there was a earthquake, or the Palisades fires, they were really good at communicating and giving us updates on how the kids are safe. The owner is a fire chief and designed all the emergency protocols. We really really love MTA, the only reason we left is because we moved to a city that's 2 hours away, otherwise, we would've stayed. On his last day, they gave us a booklet where they printed out pictures of his time there, and all the teachers wrote a little message. It's so sweet and you can tell they truly care about the kids. Thank you MTA for taking care of our lil  one, and providing such great early education and fun. Definitely enroll early as the wait list can be long.

docs.title: Review of Starting Point Mandarin Immersion Montessori Preschool
docs.text:
Google review of Starting Point Mandarin Immersion Montessori Preschool (5 out of 5, by Jin Wu, a year ago): We’ve had a fantastic experience at Starting Point Mandarin Immersion Montessori Preschool. The school offers a thoughtful blend of Montessori education and Mandarin immersion, creating a calm, nurturing, and enriching environment, with a strong emphasis on practical life skills, emotional development, and cultural awareness.

Our daughter has grown so much in independence, confidence, and language skills. The teachers are warm, attentive, and deeply committed to each child’s development. The Mandarin exposure feels natural and joyful, and we’ve been amazed at how quickly our daughter picked up vocabulary and comprehension both in Chinese and English through songs, stories, and daily conversation.

We also appreciate the open communication with families—regular updates, pictures, and school events help us feel connected to what’s happening in the classroom.

Highly recommended for families looking for a bilingual, Montessori-based early education.

docs.title: Review of Early Years School
docs.text:
Google review of Early Years School (5 out of 5, by Michael Jordan, 8 months ago): Our family has had an incredibly positive experience at The Early Years School. From the moment we joined, it was clear this is a place where children are truly seen as individuals and curiosity is genuinely celebrated.

The small class sizes and low teacher-child ratios make a huge difference. The teachers know each child deeply and meet them exactly where they are, academically, socially, and emotionally. Our child has grown more confident, more expressive, and more curious, and we see that growth reflected every day at home.

What stands out most is how thoughtfully the school supports social-emotional learning and conflict resolution. Children are guided with respect, patience, and care, learning how to communicate, problem-solve, and build empathy in a way that feels developmentally appropriate and empowering.

Beyond the classroom, The Early Years community feels like a true partnership with families. There is a strong sense of belonging, warmth, and shared values that is rare to find. We feel incredibly grateful to be part of a school that honors the “work of childhood” so intentionally and thoughtfully.

The Early Years School is a special place, and we would wholeheartedly recommend it to any family looking for a nurturing, child-centered early education experience.

docs.title: Review of Early Years School
docs.text: Google review of Early Years School (5 out of 5, by Tina B, 8 months ago): This school is a GEM in Santa Monica. Our kids loved going to school here every day. The environment they create, the teachers and staff, the way they approach young children, is all informed by research in early childhood development. I love the way they talk to and interact with the kids!! It's respectful, loving, kind and clear. This school feels like a true community. Parents all interact and are included in several events and celebrations throughout the year, and it's easy to build relationships with the teachers and one another. They really see your child and meet their needs and interests. There is a peace and calm when you enter the school and all the environments that kids love to explore. They nurture their interests and do a lot of art which we love. We toured many preschools and couldn't be happier with choosing The Early Years School!!

docs.title: Review of Palms & Paws Veterinary Center
docs.text:
Google review of Palms & Paws Veterinary Center (5 out of 5, by Haley Cohen, 5 months ago): I’ve been bringing my dog to Palms & Paws since 2023. Their consistency and quality of care keeps me coming back for nail trims, annual exams, vaccines, complex concerns, and surgical procedures. Dr. McKevilly is thoughtful, thorough, and genuinely invested in my dog’s long-term health, and provides individualized food, treat, and/or treatment recommendations based on my dog's life stage, activity level, symptoms, and occasional hunger strike.

My dog can be selectively reactive, and Dr. McKevilly consistently prioritizes his comfort by adjusting how and where procedures are done (e.g., in a private patient room and with me present, rather than main exam room in the back), and even rescheduling rather than pushing through high-stress appointments. Palms & Paws' level of awareness, patience, and flexibility with anxious dogs really sets them apart.

At Palms & Paws I've always felt fully informed, genuinely supported to choose what feels best as the owner, and never pressured into decisions. A recent example of this: in March 2026, while my dog was receiving his first dental cleaning, Dr. McKevilly personally called me mid-procedure to evaluate whether to remove his rear dewclaws at the same time (something we've discussed regularly since 2023 and extensively assessed in the weeks leading to the dental cleaning). After walking through the additional procedure step-by-step and weighing all the pros/cons of such, we determined the safest and most efficient option would be to proceed with the dewclaw removal during the dental cleaning, ultimately avoiding a second procedure with anesthesia later on or under emergency circumstances. Recovery was smooth, and the level of follow-up during healing was incredible.

Palms & Paws' follow-up care is excellent, I often hear from Dr. McKevilly the same or next day after visits, and they stay engaged daily during more complex recoveries. Highly recommend Dr. McKevilly at Palms & Paws for anyone looking for a vet who is communicative, patient, and truly cares about both the pet and the owner. I will continue to recommend Palms & Paws to family members, friends, and colleagues with different pets and will trust them with any animal I have in the future.

Google review of VCA Wilshire Animal Hospital (5 out of 5, by Echo Kilo, 7 years ago): My beloved pigeon, Clover, died on Thanksgiving Day, 2017. I hoped a full lifespan of at least 20+ years, but I am thankful for the two, amazing, but short years that she shared with me. I loved that pigeon in the same way that Nikola Tesla described his love for his pigeon.

I was speaking to my relief officer about Clover when my wife called me at 6:31 AM. "Clover died!" She wailed... I think the blood must have drained from my face because my coworker gave me an odd look.

Death is always terrible for the living, but life goes on and we have to take care of business. I wanted to get a necropsy (an animal autopsy) for Clovey because there didn't seem to be any reason for her to die. I placed her body into a box in the fridge, and I began calling veterinary clinics and hospitals. It wasn't easy to find an aviary specialist on Thanksgiving Day, so I left messages everywhere.

The first to return my call was VCA Wilshire Animal Hospital. They scheduled a necropsy with me on that day. I delivered  Clovey's body right away. I received a call from the director, Frank Lavac, DVM - who is also an aviary specialist - to talk to me about the procedure, and to discuss the follow-up. .

The doctor mentioned that the initial findings showed that she was very healthy and showed indication of trauma, and that from all initial findings there was no reason that she should have died.

Too much to go into, but pet guardians often feel like no one takes them seriously when it comes to grieving. The doctor seemed very empathetic and concerned for my well being. The staff also seemed kind and understanding when I came to pick up her remains.

Pax tibi, pulcher columbae...

Google review of VCA Santa Monica Dog and Cat Hospital (1 out of 5, by Ryan Bernard, 2 years ago): Stay far FAR away from this place. The level of incompetence at this establishment is beyond words.

My very healthy dog was given a heartworm test by Dr. Hubbard and her staff in September while on a routine visit for vaccinations. I was called the next day by Dr. Hubbard and told that my dog tested positive for heartworm, that I should keep her as still as possible, and to read up on the condition. I quickly discovered that by the time heartworm is detected by tests, it is usually too late and the condition is fatal.

I was then told by Dr. Hubbard that another test should be administered (which cost 3x as much as the first) to confirm the results. No additonal bloodwork or anything -- just another test on the same sample. I then had to wait a week to hear back, during which time I was constantly in fear of my dog dying.

The second test came back negative and I was told that the the first test "must have just been a bad test."

I asked to be refunded for the cost of the test since the lab had clearly failed to properly analyze the first one. For 5 MONTHS I tried to get the refund. All staff there, including Pattie (the hospital manager) gave nothing but excuses and illogical explanations for why I should have to pay for the tests.

3 days ago I brought my dog in for her annual wellness visit and asked about the refund again. Dr. Hubbard and the technician both avoided the issue and told me the hospital manager would call me to discuss. Their perpetually rude receptionist, Rosa, chose to argue over it instead.

docs.text:
Google review of Moon Doggy's Grooming (1 out of 5, by Cait Tegler, 4 months ago): I’ve been bringing my dog here for years, which is why this experience was especially disappointing. I got to the appointment and asked them to cut my dogs hair to a medium length. I was told my dog was “too matted” and that shaving him down was the only option. I know for a fact he was not matted, I brush him daily and can run my fingers through his fur. But shaving him down completely was probably easier and faster for the groomer so I’m sure that’s why they pushed for it.

Then a comment was made about me dropping my dog off off “sandy” because we had gone to the beach beforehand. At these grooming prices, I absolutely have the right to take my dog to the beach before bringing him in to be cleaned — that is literally the purpose of a grooming appointment. Instead of handling the situation professionally, the manager became argumentative, defensive & overly sensitive. He then threatened to refuse service while telling me to leave despite the fact that I had booked this haircut over a month in advance…and I hadn’t done anything wrong other than disagreeing that my dog was matted. This is now the second time I’ve had an issue with that same manager.

Despite this, I really needed his haircut before going away with him for the summer so I needed to keep the appointment. The manager reluctantly agreed to cut him after embarrassing me / himself in front of other customers in the lobby. When I picked my dog up, he looked terrible. They shaved him so close to the skin that he now has visible bald spots, yet somehow still left the hair around his eyes and mouth way too long and uneven.

*Another frustrating side note is that nearly every time I book an appointment online with them, they call me the day before asking if I can move the appointment to an earlier time. If they don’t actually want to honor the time slots listed on their website, then why offer them in the first place?

I immediately searched up other dog groomers to start going to in the future, and I now realize how expensive they are compared to other groomers in the area. Which is crazy considering the quality of service and customer experience. After years of coming here, I won’t be returning. Save your money and go elsewhere.

Google review of adidas Store Santa Monica (5 out of 5, by Michael Mah (MIKE MAH), 2 years ago): Downtown Santa Monica is a vibrant and diverse neighborhood that offers something for everyone. Whether you are looking for shopping, dining, entertainment, culture, or nature, you will find it here.
Some of the highlights of downtown Santa Monica are:
- The Santa Monica Pier, a historic landmark that features an amusement park, an aquarium, a carousel, and stunning views of the ocean.
- The Third Street Promenade, a pedestrian-only street that is lined with shops, restaurants, cafes, and street performers.
- The Palisades Park, a scenic park that overlooks the beach and offers walking paths, picnic areas, and a totem pole⁴.
- The Santa Monica Farmers' Market, a weekly market that showcases fresh and organic produce, flowers, baked goods, and prepared foods from local farmers and vendors.
The Santa Monica State Beach, a wide and sandy beach that is popular for sunbathing, swimming, surfing, and volleyball.
Downtown Santa Monica is also a great place to stay, as there are many hotels to choose from, ranging from budget-friendly to luxury¹¹¹². You can easily get around downtown Santa Monica by walking, biking, taking the Metro Expo Line, or using the Big Blue Bus.
Downtown Santa Monica is a place that I would recommend to anyone who wants to experience the best of Southern California. It is a place where you can enjoy the sun, the sea, and the city all in one. It is a place where you can have fun, relax, and learn something new. It is a place where you can feel the pulse of Santa Monica.

Google review of Sherwin-Williams Paint Store (1 out of 5, by Amat, 3 months ago): $67 for a gallon of basic paint before tax is outrageous.

I walked in, picked my color, and headed to the register. When I asked for the price, the employee quickly ran to the back and came back saying, “I’ll sign you up for our membership program. It’s only $67.”

Wait… that’s the membership price? So the regular price is even higher?

This wasn’t premium paint. It was a standard gallon.

Before buying it, I called Anawalt Hardware in Pacific Palisades, about a 10 minute drive away. They quoted me $43 for the exact same paint. That’s a $24 difference on a single gallon.

I walked out without buying it. The employee seemed irritated because the paint had already been mixed, but I’m not paying an extra $24 for the exact same gallon of paint. Someone else can buy it, because I refuse to overpay.

Shop around before buying paint here. A few minutes of price checking saved me a significant amount of money.

Google review of Bourget Flagstone Co. (5 out of 5, by NICK MENNELL, a year ago): If you need flagstone or lumber in Santa Monica and you DON'T go to Bourget, we can't be friends anymore.

Let me tell you about my experience: I walked in thinking I was just going to buy some rocks (fancy rocks, but still rocks), and instead I got the VIP treatment. Michelle greeted me like I was a long-lost relative who actually remembered to bring a casserole to Thanksgiving. She's absolutely lovely – patient with my million questions and somehow made flagstone selection feel less stressful than choosing a Netflix show.

Then there's Patrick, the wood-cutting wizard. This man is an ARTIST. He cut my wood with such precision I'm pretty sure he moonlights as a surgeon. Patrick, if you're reading this: you're a star. A wood-cutting, customer-service-crushing, absolute STAR. 🌟

The whole experience was so good I'm looking for excuses to buy more stone. Do I need a flagstone coffee table? Flagstone coasters? A small flagstone statue of Patrick? Who knows, but I'll be back to find out.

Highly recommend. 10/10. Would buy rocks again. Just cause.

This is the 2nd time I’ve used universal tile, and I was convinced to buy a remnant piece for my small bathroom for $255. (Back in March 2024.) I was assured their third-party contractor could install it, so I called the guy Gabriel while standing there. Sure enough he confirmed on the phone, so I paid and left.

Boy, was I wrong to do that.

Flash forward 1 week and contractor picks up the remnant piece and measures my bathroom. Then every subsequent week he rarely responds to my calls or texts for install.

2 weeks later he states the piece is too thin to cut. So I told him to return it back to universal tile. I called universal tile and they say they can’t take it, plus it’s fine to cut. So why was I getting conflicting opinions?

1 month later contractor says he’s busy. Called Universal tile and they will not give me credit or even refund. Only IF I bring the piece back. (See the pattern emerging?)

2 months later in May 2024, all my texts and calls get no response. So essentially, Contractor ghosted me and holding my piece hostage. I went to universal tile in person and complained, and they just said the same thing and were surprised they couldn’t get a hold of the contractor. (Yeah right) I asked to speak to the manager, however, she said that wasn’t necessary, and she went and talked to him. Returned and they still wouldn’t give me a refund or anything. I’m very fed up!

So unfortunately, we are now in June 2024 and I’m out $255 for nothing!! I’m never using this tile company again. I would’ve never purchased this piece if they didn’t recommend a contractor, so I believe this a scam. (I would’ve given 1 star if the bill were more expensive.)

When it came time to have the product delivered, Kesly was the liaison between myself (and I was dealing with a contractor who was dealing with the schedule of his tiling person) and the delivery company. Google review of Bank of America Financial Center (5 out of 5, by Jennifer Ciminillo, 2 months ago): I had such a great experience with Marvin at the Bank of America at 4th and Arizona in Santa Monica. My replacement debit card had accidentally been sent to my old address, and I had already been without a debit card for eight days.

Even though Marvin had an appointment coming up in just a few minutes and was trying to squeeze in a very short lunch break, he still took the time to help me. He quickly figured out what needed to be done, ordered a new card and helped expedite it so I wouldn’t have to wait even longer.

Marvin was incredibly helpful, efficient and kind — and truly a lifesaver in a frustrating situation. I really appreciated that he went out of his way to help me when he easily could have asked me to come back later. That level of customer service makes such a difference. Thank you, Marvin!

Google review of U.S. Bank Branch (1 out of 5, by Elena skaia, 5 months ago): You think you schedule an appointment and you will be helped? Oh, no silly!
I had a confirmed 12:00 PM Monday 05/11/2026 appointment.
My partner - a loyal customer since 1999 was there since before 12:00, waited in the lobby, and no one approached her (the bank was almost empty, literally 2 more people in the lobby).

When I joined her at 12:07 and we started asking for our agent, we were told that the agent had simply gone to lunch!!!
We were told they will help us but after 1pm, meaning 50 minutes later.

To make it worse, the staff (a brunette lady) told us that being 7 minutes late is "unacceptable."
They lectured us that despite the appointment was from 12:00 to 12:30 , we should have been there "12:00 sharp."
The irony is that she was actually there before 12:00, but they ignored her and then used a 7-minute "delay" as an excuse while the agent was out eating lunch.

This raises a question: does this bank actually have a policy where any minute delay results in an automatic cancellation?
We received two reminders for this appointment, yet not one of them stated that arriving any minute past the hour would forfeit my slot. The irony remains that my partner was actually there earlier, while the agent was the one who abandoned the appointment for lunch.

And, when my partner told them, "I was already here, right in front of you," and pointed out that she clearly wasn't there for the teller (since the teller windows were empty).
We asked why the agent never bothered to check if she had an appointment but just left.
The brunette agent started making ridiculous excuses, saying, "Well, we wouldn't have been able to do anything with just you anyway."
Seriously?
She didn't even know if anyone else was supposed to join my partner or what the meeting was about.
Instead of a simple apology, she offered this bizarre and, frankly, stupid excuse. What kind of logic and service is that?

I approached someone who said he is the supervisor (middle age man, gray brownish suit) and explained him the situation, but he said he cannot help and he left… I mean the supervisor physically walked out of the branch.

Then we decided to wait and at 12:29 (I was checking the time already all the time) We were sitting, talking amongst ourselves and waiting till 1pm. Yes, we decided to wait despite our busy schedule and their behaviour, we wanted to get the things done.

The blonde lady staff member approached us, no she did not come to apologize or offer some water or to actually assist…no!
She approached us…and attempted to convince us, that we arrived at 12:20…
Like…What?
One more time, we were chatting amongst ourselves already not even bothering anyone.

When we called out the lie, we mentioned that we also set up the appointment 3 days in advance and finally asked why did she even approached us, she agreed we both were there at 12:07,
but then they both (the brunette had joined and this blond lady) became hostile, accused us of being "rude," and literally started gesturing and pointing at the door to kick us out and even threatened us to „raport it” I don’t know what they were planning to report and to whom…

Please check your cameras.
You will see my partner wandering around the lobby alone with a transparent folder of documents, your supervisor walking away while we needed help, and the staff member approaching us for no reason other than to confront us.

Apparently, in this bank, being 7 minutes late is a crime, but an agent ditching a confirmed appointment for lunch is totally fine.
The supervisor who is leaving instead of taking care of the customers is totally fine.
Weird excuses, no apologies and open lie and hostility is totally fine.

I am definitely reporting this event to CFPB,BBB and OCC and so does my partner.

docs.text:
Google review of Barnes & Noble (5 out of 5, by Aaron Linsdau Thriller Author, 6 months ago): As the author of The Grant Colson Thriller Series and The SERA Archives Thriller Series, I always enjoy visiting bookstores while traveling, and Barnes & Noble is a great addition to the Santa Monica Promenade.

The store feels almost brand new and fits perfectly into the lively pedestrian shopping area along 3rd Street Promenade. The design is very clever. At first the space looks fairly compact, but there is both an upstairs and downstairs level which makes the store feel much larger once you start exploring.

When I visited, there was even a table of puzzles set up near the landing downstairs, which added a fun and welcoming touch to the space.

The layout makes excellent use of the footprint with a strong book selection and comfortable browsing areas throughout the store. While moving through the store, I ended up browsing the romance shelves as well while writing The Maui Desire Romance Series, and it’s a well-organized section that fits naturally into the layout.

The location itself is fantastic, right in the middle of the walking promenade with lots of activity and energy around it.

Parking is also relatively easy thanks to nearby parking garages, which makes visiting the promenade much simpler.

Overall it’s a beautiful new Barnes & Noble location and a great place to browse books while spending time in Santa Monica.

Google review of Barnes & Noble (5 out of 5, by Guillaume Bourcy, a year ago): My family and I treasure our visits to bookshops, especially for finding new books, birthday presents or simply browse their alleys seeking for classics. In Santa Monica, Barnes & Noble has become our preferred destination, especially given the scarce number of bookstores in downtown nowadays. The Barnes & Noble location on 3rd Street Promenade is a delightful addition and stands out as a phenomenal success.

Though it is somewhat smaller than their typical stores, this quality actually enhances its charm, making it feel more authentic and welcoming.

The layout, with two floors, thoughtfully caters to diverse interests. The lower level is wonderfully suited for younger readers, featuring a selection of toys and an impressive, well-curated collection of Mangas that we particularly enjoy. Despite its more compact size, the store does not compromise on variety, offering an extensive range of books across different genres.

What truly sets this location apart, however, is the staff. They are incredibly helpful and friendly, contributing to a sense of customer intimacy that is sometimes lost in larger spaces. It's clear that the cozy atmosphere of this smaller space fosters a closer connection between the staff and patrons.

In summary, our family's experiences at the Barnes & Noble on 3rd Street Promenade have been nothing short of wonderful. It's a gem of a bookstore that we'll continue to visit and support.

Google review of Barnes & Noble (2 out of 5, by anapat, 4 months ago): I find befuddling to have recently walked into a couple of Barnes and Nobles (Santa Monica and The Grove) and notice dozens of books on witchcraft and demons prominently displayed but had to ask an employee for the Bible section because I couldn't find it. Upon walking by some more shelves lined with books about spells and what not, at the basement and at the back, there is a little treasure trove hidden from view for only a few who bother to look for it,  inconspicuous and (perhaps) almost purposefully hidden, I find a few Bibles.

I couldn't help bringing it up to a sales associate who told me that while people pick up and browse the witchcraft books, they put them back on the shelf and told me (to my glad surprise) that Bibles actually sell better.

But then I wonder, if they sell better, should they not be displayed more prominently? Go figure.

For years I resisted buying books online to support the physical store. Even if I have to pay a little more, plus the cost of parking, I figured I was doing my part to keep them alive. Several times I drove to Barnes and Noble to pay more for a book that was cheaper on Amazon and would have been delivered to my doorstep at no charge, solely out of principle.

But seeing the kinds of books that they shove on your face while hiding what I find truly edifying and uplifting has turned me off about supporting them. But that's just me.

Google review of Zibby's Bookshop (1 out of 5, by QueeR, 5 months ago): I wanted to like Zibby’s Bookshop, but the whole thing feels less like a serious bookstore and more like a personality quiz with a cash register. The selection is limited, basic, and painfully curated, very “Instagram book club starter pack” and not especially useful for people who actually read.

The organization system is also ridiculous. Instead of normal genre sections, the shelves are arranged by “feelings” and vague life situations, like “reeling from divorce” or “into the outdoors.” Cute in theory, maybe, but in practice it feels gimmicky and unserious, like the store is more interested in branding your emotional state than helping you find a good book.

Honestly, the books feel like an afterthought. The place seems first and foremost like an event space for second-rate authors doing signing events, with a small bookstore attached to justify the vibe. If you want trendy gift books, lifestyle curation, and a place to feel literary for an afternoon, this might work. But if you care about depth, range, or a real bookstore experience, this is not it. It’s a basic bookstore for basic people.

Google review of Thunderbolt Spiritual Books (5 out of 5, by Rain Quillfrost, 4 months ago): I’ve been coming to Thunderbolt Spiritual Bookstore for about two years now, and every visit has felt consistently welcoming and genuinely enriching. The staff I’ve interacted with over time have all been kind, helpful, and easy to talk to without ever feeling performative or rushed. I also believe I’ve met the owner, who carries that same grounded, approachable energy that seems to set the tone for the whole space.

What keeps me coming back is the depth and variety of what they offer. Their selection of tarot and oracle decks is extensive, and I’ve found several that I still use regularly. I’ve also purchased crystals, stones, books, and fragrances there, and I’ve always left feeling satisfied with what I chose. The $5 books outside the store are especially special to me, since they include such a wide range that I would not have discovered on my own. Many of them look practically new, and I’ve ended up reading things I never would have picked up otherwise, which has been genuinely eye-opening. I also appreciate being able to gift some of those books forward. It’s a place that feels like it keeps knowledge circulating in a really accessible way, and I hope it continues to stay exactly as it is for a long time.
